summary: Six-lens expert review of the new-repo master design against field best practice

reports.lens: Lens 1 — Data standards and pipeline architecture (neurophysiology data infrastructure)
reports.overall_verdict: The design is a strong, unusually self-aware piece of *software* engineering — the generated identity registry (ADR-004), the append-only attributed decision log (ADR-011), the execution-log-is-authoritative provenance rule (S5), and the explained-difference gate (ADR-009) are at or above what most systems-neuroscience labs do, and ADR-009 is better than the bit-identity reproduction gate a naive rebuild would adopt. But it has one structural blind spot that is large enough to undermine several of its own guarantees: **the data layer itself is never specified.** `grep -niE "pickle|\.pkl|nwb|hdf5|parquet|zarr|datajoint|spyglass|checksum|hash|schema.version"` over both the master design and the sub-project 0 audit spec returns exactly one hit, and it is an unrelated mention of `state_rule.pkl`. The design therefore silently inherits: uncompressed Python pickle as the 30.5 GB session store (with a 10-branch `RenamingUnpickler` at `core/session.py:197-236` proving the coupling is already load-bearing), untyped CSV as the derived-artefact format (539 CSVs, 0 parquet — CSV's int64 round-trip is the *mechanism* of the 15,802 corrupted session-id rows, so ADR-004's typed IDs fix it in memory and nothing fixes it on disk), 16,131 bare `.npy` files with no axis or unit metadata, a `Cluster` record carrying only `cluster_id/spike_times/quality` so that every per-unit attribute (anatomy, waveform, tracking, cell type) must be string-joined back in, no schema version on any artefact despite demonstrable schema drift (`session.py:52-58`), no content hash of any input, and a silent fall-back to *uncorrected spike times* at `ingest.py:242-257` that the artefact does not record. My core recommendation is not "adopt a framework": DataJoint/Spyglass are correctly rejected for a solo Windows+Slurm project mid-paper. It is that the new repo must specify a **self-describing, schema-versioned, content-hashed session artefact** — I recommend NWB/HDF5, written via NeuroConv, behind a `SessionStore` boundary — because the design's own principle ("every definition exists exactly once, divergence mechanically prevented") is currently applied to code and not to data, and the project's worst measured defects (lick-channel re-extraction, stale TF registries, corrupted joins, pre-TPrime staleness) all live on the data side.
matches_best_practice: ADR-004 (generated registry as the sole authority for identity, typed SubjectID/SessionKey downstream) is the right diagnosis and the right cure. It buys most of what Spyglass/DataJoint get from a relational schema — a single canonical key domain — without a database server. Keep it.

ADR-011's append-only, attributed decision log with staging manifests as *generated build artefacts* actually exceeds DataJoint/Spyglass practice: in those systems the roster is mutable DB state, and 'who excluded this session and why' is not versioned unless you build it. Recording the reason as a required field is better than the field standard.

S5's rule that the execution log outranks the recorded code where they disagree is sharper than what most provenance systems assert, and matches the failure this project actually had (scripts whose stated behaviour diverged from what ran). Most provenance tooling (DVC, DataLad rerun) records the *invocation*; asserting log-over-code precedence is the correct tiebreak.

ADR-002/S8 (layered install, `pip install -e .[analysis]` with no UnitMatch/GPU/MATLAB) matches how SpikeInterface and Spyglass ship — heavy sorters and curation stacks behind extras. Rare in single-lab repos and worth the maintenance.

ADR-009's explained-difference gate is a better port gate than numerical equivalence, and its reasoning (a substantial fraction of old outputs are known-wrong, so reproduction would encode defects) is exactly right for a repo with a measured 12-defect register.

ADR-014 (null control + synthetic parameter recovery as *gates*, not habits) exceeds field norm; most labs treat recovery on ground truth as optional. Keeping `utils/synthetic.py` load-bearing is the correct call.

The sub-project 0 rule 'measured, not read' — with `load_qc_profile()` returning `{}` as the worked example — is the right defence against ADR-006's big-design-up-front risk, and is what makes the spec-first choice defensible.

proposals.target: NEW-ADR (ADR-015) — Canonical session artefact: self-describing, schema-versioned, NWB/HDF5
proposals.title: Replace pickle with NWB (HDF5 backend) as the canonical session store, written via NeuroConv, behind a SessionStore boundary
proposals.detail: Specify the session artefact explicitly: an NWB file per session carrying (a) `NWBFile.identifier` + `session_id` + `Subject.subject_id` as stamped identity, (b) a `trials` TimeIntervals table with custom columns (`change_size`, `trialoutcome`, `change_time`, RT dict flattened), (c) a `Units` DynamicTable with spike times plus all per-unit metadata, (d) NI events as `LabeledEvents`/`TimeSeries`, and (e) the per-frame stimulus log as a session-continuous TimeSeries (TF, phase, vbl) with a trial-index column rather than ragged per-trial arrays. Ingest uses NeuroConv's SpikeGLX and Phy/KiloSort interfaces rather than the hand-rolled `.npy` reader. Put the whole thing behind a `SessionStore` interface with one `load_session(SessionKey) -> Session` entry point so the backend is swappable and the analysis layer (ported per ADR-001) is untouched. Reject NWB-Zarr for now — NWB documents HDF5 as the primary backend and Zarr as immature for multi-language, many-small-files transfer; revisit only if cloud/parallel access becomes a need. Fallback if the frame log proves awkward: NWB for units/trials/events plus a referenced Parquet sidecar, still under the same boundary.
proposals.rationale: Pickle couples 30.5 GB of irreplaceable derived data to a Python module layout that has already moved: `core/session.py:197-236` carries a `RenamingUnpickler` with ten remap branches plus a bare `except Exception: pickle.load(f)` at :238-242, and `save_session` (:253-256) is a raw `pickle.dump` with no protocol pin, no compression and no schema field. Every load is all-or-nothing, which is why CLAUDE.md has to mandate `del sess; gc.collect()` — a memory rule that is really a format artefact; 85-196 MB per session is read in full to touch a handful of units. NWB gives lazy per-column/per-unit reads, compression (likely 30 GB -> ~10 GB), free validation via nwbinspector, DANDI eligibility, and — decisively for this project — puts the data in the same format and API as the Allen Visual Behavior Neuropixels dataset (153 sessions, 81 mice, *the same visual change-detection paradigm*), which is the natural public comparator for a multi-subject learning paper. Adopting a standard also avoids the design's own trap: a bespoke internal schema is a new single source of truth that can drift, which is exactly what ADR-005 exists to prevent.
proposals.evidence: e:/python_analysis/git_repos/vis_detect_analysis_Sep2025/src/visdetect/core/session.py:197-256; data measured: 285 pkls, 85-196 MB each (ls -la data/pkls/BG_046/). https://nwb.org/convert/ ; https://neuroconv.readthedocs.io/en/main/ ; https://github.com/catalystneuro/neuroconv ; https://nwb-overview.readthedocs.io/en/latest/faq_details/why_hdf5.html ; https://allensdk.readthedocs.io/en/latest/visual_behavior_neuropixels.html ; https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10335829/

proposals.target: Sub-project 0 audit spec §3.2 — new domain D9 (or D4 extension): storage-format spike
proposals.title: Time-boxed executable spike: convert 3 real sessions to NWB and measure size, read latency and round-trip equality before ADR-015 is finalised
proposals.detail: Add one measured deliverable to the audit: convert three sessions spanning the range (a small BG_049, a large BG_046 September session, and a BG_012 twin with colliding date keys) to NWB via NeuroConv; report compressed size vs pkl, cold-read latency for the three access patterns the analysis layer actually uses (all trials for one unit; all units in one time window; the trials table alone), round-trip equality of spike times and trials against the pkl, and where the per-frame stim log lands. Cap it at one working day. Record the result in `measurements.csv` so ADR-015 cites a number rather than an expectation.
proposals.rationale: ADR-006 puts all risk on specification, and the audit's own defining rule is 'measured, not read'. The storage-format decision is precisely the kind of claim that reads as obvious and can be wrong in execution — pynwb read latency for per-trial, per-unit access is the one real risk in proposal 1, and it is cheap to settle now versus discovering it in sub-project 3. This does not relitigate ADR-006; it is the same empirical-grounding mitigation ADR-006 already commits to, applied to the one layer the audit currently does not measure at all.
proposals.evidence: docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-06-subproject-0-audit-spec.md §3 rule 3 ('Measured, not read') and §4 deliverable 4 (`measurements.csv`); the audit's D4 covers cache/figure provenance but never measures the pkl store itself.

proposals.target: NEW-ADR (ADR-016) or ADR-004 extension — registry rows carry content hashes of every upstream input and produced artefact
proposals.title: Content-hash the inputs: a registry snapshot names paths, and the project's worst defect changed content at unchanged paths
proposals.detail: Every registry row must carry sha256 + byte size + mtime for each upstream input (the `*trials.json` set, the `*NIdaq_events.mat`, a manifest hash over the Kilosort output directory, the TPrime-adjusted spike-times file) and for the produced session artefact. Registry refresh diffs hashes against the previous revision and emits a `changed-inputs` report that must be acknowledged in the decision log (ADR-011) before downstream artefacts are considered valid. S5's 'inputs' component becomes 'registry snapshot + decision-log revision + input content digests', not paths alone.
proposals.rationale: The lick-channel defect is the proof: a MATLAB re-extraction on 6 Mar 2026 changed the content of the NI event files for 33 sessions, under-detecting licks by 10-40x, at unchanged paths. A registry snapshot recording paths would have been byte-identical before and after; nothing in S5 as written would have flagged it. The same applies to the BG_031 re-sort and the BG_041/049 pkl rebuilds visible in `data/*.log`. This single mechanism converts an entire class of silent upstream mutation into a build event, and it is the cheapest high-value addition in this review.
proposals.evidence: memory/new_repo_rebuild_aug2026.md defect #12 and lick_channel_defect_jul2026; src/visdetect/core/ingest.py load_ni_events reads `*NIdaq_events.mat` produced outside the repo; data/bg031_reextract.log, data/bg041_049_pkl_rebuild.log; master design S5 lists inputs as 'registry snapshot + decision-log revision'.

proposals.target: NEW-ADR (ADR-017) or ADR-004 extension — time-base provenance is mandatory and the uncorrected fallback is not silent
proposals.title: Record the clock-correction provenance in the artefact and refuse to serve spike times whose time base is unknown
proposals.detail: `load_kilosort_spikes` currently tries `spike_times_sec_adj.npy` (TPrime-corrected), then `spike_times_sec.npy`, then `spike_times.npy / sample_rate`, logging the choice at INFO and recording nothing in the Session — so a pre-TPrime session is byte-indistinguishable from a corrected one downstream. `build_concat_pkls.py:225` has the same silent fallback. Specify that the session artefact carries a `time_base` block (which file was used, TPrime version/build, reference stream, sync-edge residual statistics), that ingest *fails* rather than falls back, and that an uncorrected session can only be built with an explicit flag that stamps `time_base="uncorrected"` — after which the loader refuses to serve it unless the calling analysis declares that intent (the same guard pattern ADR-012 already builds for the `cohort` field).
proposals.rationale: This is the most safety-critical transform in the pipeline and the one the project has already been burned by: 'pre-TPrime = STALE, do NOT use for new analyses' is a CLAUDE.md gotcha, and 'TPrime-first' is recorded as a lesson from the BG_031 re-extraction. Today that rule is enforced by a directory name (`preTprime/`) and human memory. An untracked script `scripts/QC_technical/validate_event_spike_clock_drift.py` sitting in the working tree shows this is a live concern. The design's registry types *identity* but nothing types the *time base*, and every alignment, PETH and latency result in the project depends on it.
proposals.evidence: src/visdetect/core/ingest.py:242-257 (three-branch fallback, logger.info only); scripts/pipelines/concat_sort/build_concat_pkls.py:225 ('TPrime: unavailable — using uncorrected times'); CLAUDE.md gotcha 'pre-TPrime = stale'; memory/bg031_reextract_inprogress_jun2026 'TPrime-first lesson'; untracked scripts/QC_technical/validate_event_spike_clock_drift.py in git status.

proposals.target: ADR-011 extension / sub-project 4 spec — derived artefacts are content-addressed, not merely provenanced
proposals.title: Provenance records what produced an artefact; it does not stop you using a stale one. Add content-addressed cache keys.
proposals.detail: Specify that every derived artefact's filename or sidecar key is a hash of (producing module's code version + the constants it reads + input content digests + parameters), and that the loader *refuses* to return a cache whose recomputed key does not match. Where recomputation is expensive, the loader may serve the stale artefact only with an explicit `allow_stale=` declaration that is recorded in the results ledger row (ADR-013). This is the one genuinely valuable idea to take from DataJoint/Spyglass — dependency-driven invalidation — delivered without a database.
proposals.rationale: S5 makes artefacts *traceable* but nothing in the design makes them *invalid*. The audit's own examples are all staleness, not missing provenance: the three `tf_responsive` registries whose own README says STALE are still loaded with no gate after the 2026-08-03 lick fix and they gate the VMS 5.3% > DMS 2.8/3.1% headline; `predicted_session_groups.csv` holds `chron` values current code cannot produce. Adding a sidecar to those files would have documented the staleness without preventing its use. Content-addressing makes 'the inputs changed' a hard failure at read time.
proposals.evidence: memory/new_repo_rebuild_aug2026.md defects #6 and #12; audit spec D4 'Per-cache staleness: mtime vs last-commit ... validated by a schema/value check (the predicted_session_groups.csv chron column is the worked example)'; https://ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC10849637 (Spyglass: 'results are automatically updated when the data or analysis code changes').

proposals.target: NEW-ADR (ADR-018) or ADR-015 §units — canonical per-session Units table
proposals.title: Fold all per-unit metadata into the session artefact's Units table; stop joining anatomy, waveform, tracking and cell type by string keys
proposals.detail: The `Cluster` record carries only `cluster_id`, `spike_times`, `quality`. Everything else that the science depends on — peak channel, depth, CCF region, waveform metrics, Bombcell/curation features, UnitMatch and DANT tracked ids, optotag verdict, cell-type label, TF hand-labels — lives in separate per-topic caches under `data/cache/{anatomy,curation_features*,dant,tracking_consensus,tf_labeling,optotagging}` joined on `(session_id, cluster_id)` strings. Specify one canonical Units table per session (NWB `Units` DynamicTable), where each derived column carries its own `*_version` and `*_source` attribute. Downstream code selects columns; it never joins by string key. A `UnitID` type (subject + session + cluster_id) sits alongside `SubjectID`/`SessionKey` in ADR-004's typed API.
proposals.rationale: The (session_id, cluster_id) string join is the exact surface on which the 15,802 corrupted-row defect operates, and the design fixes only half of it: ADR-004 types the session id in memory but leaves the join itself as the architecture. Making per-unit metadata columns of one table rather than rows of eight files makes the whole class of misjoin structurally impossible, and it is how NWB and Spyglass model units. It also removes the `int(cluster_id)` dtype hazard that mirrors the session-id one.
proposals.evidence: src/visdetect/core/session.py:37-41 (Cluster fields); data/cache/ listing shows anatomy/, curation_features_BG_*.pkl, dant/, tracking_consensus/, tf_labeling/, optotagging/, um_ref/ as separate join targets; memory defect #1 (15,802 corrupted rows across 6 caches).

proposals.target: ADR-011 extension / sub-project 4 spec — tabular artefact format
proposals.title: Derived tabular artefacts are Parquet; CSV is an export format only. This kills the leading-zero bug at the format level.
proposals.detail: Mandate Parquet (or any typed columnar format) for every derived table the pipeline reads back, with CSV permitted only as a terminal human-readable export that no code re-reads. Similarly, ban bare `.npy` for derived arrays: array artefacts go into a per-analysis HDF5/Zarr group (or an `.npz` with a mandatory metadata member) carrying named dimensions, bin centres, unit ids and window definitions as attributes. Add a gate that fails on `pd.read_csv` of a path under the cache root.
proposals.rationale: The leading-zero session-id bug is not a discipline failure, it is a *format* failure: CSV has no dtype, so an all-numeric `session_name` column round-trips to int64 and `01072025` becomes `1072025`. ADR-004's typed IDs fix this in memory; nothing in the design fixes it on disk, and the measured state is 539 CSVs and 0 Parquet under `data/cache`. Parquet preserves the string dtype and makes the defect unreachable. The 16,131 bare `.npy` files are the same problem for arrays: an anonymous float array with no bin centres or unit ordering cannot be validated or reused, and silently mis-indexes if the producing code's ordering changes.
proposals.evidence: Measured under e:/python_analysis/git_repos/vis_detect_analysis_Sep2025/data/cache: 539 *.csv, 0 *.parquet, 16,131 *.npy/*.npz, 0 *.h5. CLAUDE.md gotcha: 'Never write session_name to CSV as an int column — it round-trips back to int64 and drops the zero'. memory defect #1 and #6.

proposals.target: ADR-004 — identity is stamped into the data at ingest, not only derived from filenames in one place
proposals.title: Make the registry's primary key opaque and immutable, and stamp it inside the artefact so mis-naming is detectable rather than re-derivable
proposals.detail: ADR-004 correctly makes the registry the sole place identity is *derived* from filenames — but identity still ultimately lives in a filename, so a rename, a copy, or a re-ingest can re-key a session with no error. Change the model: at ingest, assign an immutable opaque `session_uid` (never the date, never the filename), write it plus `subject_id` and `schema_version` *inside* the artefact, and make the registry an index over stamped ids. Loading validates that the path-derived key and the stamped key agree; disagreement is a hard error, not a re-derivation. NWB gives this for free via `NWBFile.identifier` / `session_id` / `Subject.subject_id`, and DANDI already requires a `Subject` with `subject_id`, so adopting proposal 1 satisfies this at no extra cost.
proposals.rationale: BG_012 has nine colliding date keys and a 49-rows-for-40-dates manifest, and the `_b`/`_c`/`_v2` twins are re-sorts of identical behaviour that must never be concatenated. A date-derived key cannot express that; a `variant` field attached to a date-derived key still lets a re-ingest reshuffle which twin is which. An opaque stamped id makes the twin problem a data fact rather than a naming convention, and makes 'this file is not the session the registry thinks it is' a detectable condition — which is currently impossible.
proposals.evidence: master design ADR-004 ('the only place identity is derived from filenames'); audit spec §8 resolved-question 3 (BG_012 in full scope: '9 colliding date-keys and 49-rows-for-40-dates'); memory/suffixed_session_files_aug2026; https://docs.dandiarchive.org/user-guide-sharing/validating-files/ (Subject with subject_id required).

proposals.target: ADR-015 §schema — mandatory schema_version and explicit migrations
proposals.title: Version the data schema, and stop conflating 'field absent' with 'field null'
proposals.detail: Every session artefact carries a `schema_version`; the loader refuses versions it does not know; schema changes ship with an explicit, tested migration and a decision-log entry. Ban the current pattern where a new field is added with a plain `None` default so that old artefacts silently read as null: `trial_event_index` is documented as 'None = alignment not yet verified', with a code comment explaining the default must be plain `None` because pkls written before the field existed would otherwise raise AttributeError — so 'never verified' and 'this version predates verification' are the same value. `stim_phase`/`stim_tf_disp`/`stim_vbl` have the identical shape ('All None on legacy pkls until backfilled').
proposals.rationale: This is the rebuild's own thesis — one definition, divergence mechanically prevented — applied to data instead of code, and the current store already demonstrates the drift. The specific hazard is scientific, not cosmetic: a downstream analysis that treats `trial_event_index is None` as 'no alignment needed' rather than 'alignment unverified' produces plausible wrong numbers, which the design correctly identifies as this codebase's characteristic failure mode. A version field plus an explicit backfill state makes the distinction representable.
proposals.evidence: src/visdetect/core/session.py:52-58 (trial_event_index, with the AttributeError comment) and :31-35 (stim_phase/stim_tf_disp/stim_vbl 'All None on legacy pkls until backfilled'); master design contains zero occurrences of 'schema version' (grep).

proposals.target: ADR-004 and ADR-011 — record the considered-and-rejected external frameworks
proposals.title: Name DataJoint / DataJoint Elements array-ephys and Spyglass in the Alternatives sections, and record why they are rejected
proposals.detail: Both ADRs list only hand-rolled alternatives, so a reader (or reviewer) cannot tell whether the field-standard options were considered. Add them with the honest accounting: Spyglass would require converting to NWB (it consumes NWB only), running a MySQL server, and re-expressing every analysis as DataJoint computed tables — a full rewrite of the layer ADR-001 explicitly decided to *port*, not re-derive. DataJoint Elements array-ephys assumes a Kilosort-centric pipeline and a live database; its tutorials run against a local MySQL that resets between sessions, which is real operational overhead on Windows for one person. Record that the two ideas worth stealing are adopted separately: NWB as the store (proposal 1) and dependency-driven invalidation (proposal 5).
proposals.rationale: These are the exact tools a reviewer or a future collaborator will ask about, and the current ADRs give no evidence they were weighed. Recording the rejection with reasons costs one paragraph and protects the decision from being relitigated every time someone reads the design. It also makes the two borrowed ideas legible as deliberate borrowings rather than reinvention.
proposals.evidence: master design ADR-004 Alternatives (a)-(c) and ADR-011 Alternatives (a)-(c) — all hand-rolled; https://ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC10849637 and https://elifesciences.org/reviewed-preprints/108089 (Spyglass = NWB + DataJoint + relational DB); https://github.com/datajoint/element-array-ephys ; https://docs.datajoint.com/elements/element-array-ephys/latest/tutorials/ (local MySQL that resets between sessions).

proposals.target: Sub-project 1 spec (Foundation) — ingest reader test corpus and upstream tool-version recording
proposals.title: Raw readers get committed tiny fixtures with golden outputs, and record the version of every upstream tool in the artefact
proposals.detail: Commit a minimal real-data fixture set: one truncated SpikeGLX `.meta`, a ~200-trial `trials.json`, a 50-spike Kilosort directory (`spike_times*.npy`, `spike_clusters.npy`, `params.py`, `cluster_group.tsv`), and a small `NIdaq_events.mat` — each with a golden expected output, so every reader is testable offline in CI (this is also what makes S8's `pip install -e .[analysis]` claim checkable). Separately, parse and record upstream versions into the artefact: SpikeGLX version from the `.meta` header, Kilosort version from `params.py`/ops, the TPrime build, and the sha of the MATLAB NI-extraction script. Prefer NeuroConv's SpikeGLX/Phy interfaces over the hand-rolled `.npy` loader so format drift is someone else's maintenance burden.
proposals.rationale: The design puts ingest in the repo and layers it first, but says nothing about how readers are tested or how upstream tool versions are captured — and the reproducible-pipelines literature is explicit that a complete record of parameters and versions is the requirement, not the code alone. Concretely, this is what would have made the lick-channel re-extraction visible: the artefact would have recorded which extraction script produced its NI events. Fixtures also make the readers the *cheapest* part of the ADR-007 approval process rather than the most argued-about.
proposals.evidence: src/visdetect/core/ingest.py (hand-rolled Kilosort/`params.py`/`cluster_group.tsv` readers), src/visdetect/core/spikeglx.py:81; https://elifesciences.org/articles/110170 (SpikeInterface reproducible pipelines: complete record of code and reported parameters); https://neuroconv.readthedocs.io/en/main/ (SpikeGLX and KiloSort/Phy interfaces).

proposals.target: ADR-002 / sub-project 1 spec — declare the MATLAB NI-extraction an external upstream artefact or bring it in-repo
proposals.title: The design implies MATLAB is out of the pipeline; it is not — NI events still come from a MATLAB-produced .mat at the root of ingest
proposals.detail: `load_ni_events` reads `*NIdaq_events.mat` from `Processed data/<session>/Nidaq/`, produced by MATLAB code outside the repo. Either (a) read the raw SpikeGLX `.nidq.bin` digital/analog channels directly in Python — `core/spikeglx.py` already exists and the project's own note says the raw SpikeGLX data is fine while the re-extraction is broken — or (b) explicitly declare the `.mat` an external upstream artefact with a recorded producer identity, version and content hash (proposal 3). Whichever is chosen, the master design must name it, because right now the ingest layer has an unversioned MATLAB dependency at its root and the repo's own defect register says that dependency is currently wrong for 33 sessions.
proposals.rationale: `ingest.py`'s docstring claims it 'Replaces the MATLAB loadSessionNPX_main.m pipeline', which is only true for behaviour and spikes. The one part still on MATLAB is the part with the known 10-40x defect, and the layered-repo design (ADR-002) does not have a place for it. Option (a) also permanently retires the defect rather than versioning around it.
proposals.evidence: src/visdetect/core/ingest.py docstring lines 1-12 and load_ni_events (reads `*NIdaq_events.mat` via scipy.io.loadmat); src/visdetect/core/spikeglx.py; memory/lick_channel_defect_jul2026 ('ROOT CAUSE: Piezo/Lick split = MATLAB RE-EXTRACTION (6 Mar 2026, 33 sess) UNDER-DETECTS licks 10-40x; raw SpikeGLX fine').

proposals.target: NEW-ADR (ADR-019) — chronic unit identity is typed and versioned
proposals.title: Add ChronicUnitID alongside SubjectID/SessionKey, and own the fact that NWB has no standard for cross-session unit identity
proposals.detail: Cross-session tracking (UnitMatch, DANT, the 312-neuron consensus cohort) is this project's signature capability, yet the identity model stops at the session boundary. Add a `ChronicUnitID` type carried as a Units-table column, storing the tracker name and version, the match score, and the consensus rule that produced it; a gate bans bare `(session, cluster)` tuples in public signatures the same way ADR-004 bans bare session ids. Record explicitly that NWB has no accepted representation for cross-session unit identity, so this is a project-owned custom column (candidate for a small `ndx-` extension later if the data is published) — and that the tracker version must be part of the key, since UnitMatch 3.2.9 and the curated tracker disagree (AUC 0.96 vs 0.64).
proposals.rationale: The project already measured that 'tracked' can mean different things depending on tracker and curation, and that bimodal cross-session ISI in nominally tracked units is a matching failure. If chronic identity remains an untyped CSV join keyed on the same strings that produced the 15,802-row defect, the multi-subject learning analyses — which are inherently across-session — inherit the weakest link in the identity model that ADR-004 was written to fix.
proposals.evidence: memory/neuron_tracking_may2026 (UM 3.2.9 vs track-curation AUC 0.96 vs 0.64), memory/tracking_qc_bimodal_isi_finding, memory/consensus_cohort_optotagging_figs_jul2026 (312-neuron UM∩DANT consensus); data/cache/{tracking_consensus,tracking_dant,um_ref}/ as separate join targets; web search found no NWB standard for cross-session unit tracking (https://researchdata.springernature.com/posts/61202-challenges-in-utilizing-the-neurodata-without-borders-nwb-format-for-human-single-unit-data).

proposals.title: Commit to NWB export + DANDI as a paper-time deliverable, but protect it now with a CI round-trip test
proposals.detail: Do not spend effort on DANDI metadata completeness now. Do add, from day one, a CI test that writes one small synthetic session through the artefact writer and runs `nwbinspector --config dandi` over it, asserting zero CRITICAL findings — since only CRITICAL findings block a DANDI upload. That keeps the export path from rotting for the two years before deposition, at roughly ten lines of test code, and means the eventual deposition is a metadata-filling exercise rather than a conversion project.
proposals.rationale: Data deposition is increasingly a condition of publication and of Wellcome/UKRI-funded work, and DANDI accepts NWB only. Doing the conversion at paper time under deadline is where conversions go wrong; doing it now is premature. A standing validator test is the cheap middle path, and it also acts as a schema regression test for proposal 1 independently of any publication plan.
proposals.evidence: https://docs.dandiarchive.org/user-guide-sharing/validating-files/ (nwbinspector --config dandi; only CRITICAL findings block upload); https://docs.dandiarchive.org/getting-started/data-standards/nwb/ ; https://nwb-overview.readthedocs.io/en/latest/conversion_tutorial/06_dandi.html

overbuilt: Sub-project 0's traceability census over *every* tracked FIGURES artefact (3,056 figures / 36 GB) is more work than the answer is worth — the recon already measured that only 43 of 183 figure-writing scripts import `config.FIGURE_DIR` and stem-matching succeeds 14% of the time. A stratified sample of ~100 figures gives the same headline fraction with a confidence interval, in a fraction of the time. The census's stated purpose is 'evidence for the provenance layer, not a target' (audit spec D4), and a sample is sufficient evidence for that purpose.

Do not adopt DataJoint, DataJoint Elements or Spyglass. Spyglass requires NWB *plus* MySQL *plus* re-expressing analyses as DataJoint computed tables — a full rewrite of exactly the layer ADR-001 decided to port rather than re-derive. For one person on Windows with a paper to finish, the database is pure operational overhead. Take the two ideas (NWB store; dependency-driven invalidation) and leave the framework.

If proposal 1 (NWB) is adopted, do NOT also write and maintain a bespoke internal data-schema specification. One store, one schema, owned upstream. A parallel in-house schema document would recreate the exact 'same definition in two places' failure the rebuild exists to cure, in the data layer.

ADR-007 approval packets applied per-reader would produce four or five near-identical packets for `load_behavioral_trials`, `load_kilosort_spikes`, `load_ni_events`, `load_mat_file_to_session`. Collapse these into one 'raw readers' packet whose 'how we know it's right' section is the golden-fixture test suite output (proposal 11) — the executed-output requirement is satisfied better by one fixture run over all readers than by four hand-written arguments.

Running the old 30.5 GB pkl store and a new store simultaneously through the whole port doubles storage on the same disk that the June-2026 data-loss incident happened on. Add an explicit sub-project 6 step: after the ADR-009 comparison is complete, record the pkl inventory with sha256 digests in the registry, verify the new store round-trips, then delete the pkls. Keeping both indefinitely is the expensive default, not the safe one.
open_questions: Does the target journal or the funder (Wellcome/UKRI via UCL) require data deposition for the multi-subject paper? If yes, NWB stops being optional and proposal 1 becomes a hard requirement rather than an architectural preference — worth settling before ADR-015 is written, because it changes the cost calculus entirely.

How should the per-frame stimulus log (`stim_phase` (n_frames,2), `stim_tf_disp`, `stim_vbl` per trial) be represented? A session-continuous frame table with a trial-index column is cleaner and more correct than ragged per-trial arrays, but it changes how the TF-GLM code indexes. This is the one genuine schema-design decision in proposal 1 and the storage spike (proposal 2) should answer it with a measurement.

Is `scripts/pipelines/concat_sort/build_concat_pkls.py` a supported v1 ingest path? It has its own TPrime handling with the same silent fallback (:225) and its own session-construction logic — if it stays, it must meet the same time-base and hashing guarantees; if it is dropped, that belongs on `drop-list.md`.

Are UnitMatch and DANT outputs recomputed inside the new repo or ingested as frozen upstream artefacts? They are expensive and GPU/MATLAB-adjacent, which argues for ingest-as-artefact with recorded tracker version and hash — but that makes `ChronicUnitID` an *input* rather than a derived quantity, which changes where it sits in the layer graph (ADR-002).

If NWB compression takes the session store from ~30 GB to roughly 10 GB, does a second copy on HPC scratch or a Slurm-accessible filesystem become feasible? That would give genuine off-disk redundancy for data currently protected only by a same-disk copy — which sub-project -1 explicitly flags as accidental-deletion protection only, not disk-failure protection.

What is the intended lifetime of `data/cache`'s 16,131 `.npy` files across the migration? Under proposal 7 they are not portable (no axis metadata), so either they are regenerated in the new repo or they are dropped — and if any of them back a hardened result, that regeneration is on the ADR-009 critical path.

reports.overall_verdict: This design's scientific-correctness layer is, on paper, ahead of most systems-neuroscience labs: git-committed pre-specification with a falsifier and a minimum interesting effect, a pseudoreplication declaration as a contract row, effect-size-plus-CI as a required ledger field, retracted/refuted as first-class statuses, and null controls promoted from norm to build gate. Almost nobody CI-enforces any of that. The gaps are not of ambition but of specification: the pseudoreplication gate as worded ("mixed-effects wherever n_units >> n_sessions >> n_subjects") will silently license subject-as-random-effect at k=3, where the variance component is unestimable and the model returns pooled inference wearing a rigorous hat; "the null must be flat" has no quantitative criterion, no dependency-respecting shuffle spec, and no permutation-count floor; and parameter recovery without model recovery does not license the project's actual headline claims, which are model-comparison claims (drift vs threshold, K states, number of population dimensions). The forking-paths admission in ADR-012 is honest but leaves the mitigation entirely to visibility, when a bounded, pre-declared specification curve on confirmed claims only is genuinely affordable here — and becomes nearly free if ADR-010's scaffold requires every analytic degree of freedom to be a parameter rather than a literal, which is the same architectural move S1 already mandates. Three things are missing outright: an equivalence-testing route so the project's honest negatives can say "we can exclude effects larger than X" rather than just "n.s."; RNG seed, resample counts and resampling unit in the S5 provenance sidecar (a fixed global seed=42 across all analyses is in the old CLAUDE.md and is both a reuse hazard and unrecorded); and any design-sensitivity calculation to tell the project how many more subjects buy what. One sequencing error matters: the lab's strongest scientific instrument, the harden-result battery, is prose in the AI layer (sub-project 5, built last), so the analysis port in sub-project 3 happens without it.
matches_best_practice: ADR-010's pre-specification row (prediction + falsifier + minimum interesting effect, committed to git before the run) is timestamped preregistration at zero marginal cost — the single cheapest reform most labs still don't do.

ADR-014 making null controls a build gate rather than a habit exceeds field standard; the stated rationale (a rule that depends on remembering to apply it fails exactly when the result is exciting) is correct and is exactly why the TF-pulse circularity bug shipped.

ADR-013's `retracted`/`refuted` statuses with a `superseded by` pointer are better than what most labs do, where retractions vanish into a lab notebook. Keeping them visible is a trustworthiness asset, not an embarrassment.

Requiring effect size + CI in the same ledger row as the claim, with the explicit statement that a p-value alone is not a result, is the right call at n = thousands of units where p < 0.001 is available for biologically meaningless effects.

ADR-010's pseudoreplication declaration as a contract requirement puts the project ahead of the ~53% of neuroscience studies that have nested data and analyse it as independent (https://www.biorxiv.org/content/10.1101/819334v2.full).

ADR-009's explained-difference gate is statistically the right target: bit-reproduction of an old pipeline whose QC profiles silently no-op would enforce known-wrong numbers, while a pure fresh build would make an accidental regression indistinguishable from an intended fix.
ADR-012's explicit written statement of what within-analysis CV does not protect against is unusually candid and technically correct — most papers imply cross-validation solves multiplicity.

Within-analysis holdout already mandatory for decoders, and coding directions computed on training folds and projected on held-out data, match the project's own methods corpus (normalize-before-reduce, never test on training data).

proposals.title: Bounded, pre-declared specification curve — for `confirmed` claims only, made cheap by parameterisation
proposals.detail: Add a contract row: every analysis declares, before running, the 3-6 analytic degrees of freedom whose alternatives are equally defensible (QC/firing-rate threshold, unit-selection path, baseline window, smoothing sigma, session-inclusion filter, trial-matching scheme, session-ordering axis). Enforce mechanically by requiring each declared DoF to be a keyword argument defaulting to a registry constant, never an inline literal — the gates of sub-project 2 already ban inline magic numbers, so this is the same check pointed at a new purpose. When and only when a ledger row is promoted to `confirmed`, run the factorial over declared DoFs and report the specification curve: median effect, fraction of specs same-sign, fraction significant, and Simonsohn's step-3 joint inference under a permutation null — the inferential step most users skip, without which the curve is decorative. Exploratory rows are explicitly exempt, so exploration is not taxed.
proposals.rationale: The design admits cross-analysis multiplicity is unmitigated except by visibility. A curve over pre-declared choices converts 'we could have done it 40 ways' from an unknowable into a plotted quantity, and the project has a concrete instance waiting: session ordering (calendar date vs trials-completed vs d-prime stage vs blinded-sorter label) drives every learning-slope claim, and the current parse bug already proves ordering is not a settled choice. Cost is real but bounded: on cached session-level statistics a 48-200 spec curve is minutes; only refit-requiring axes (QC threshold, unit selection) need a coarse 3-point sweep rather than a full factorial.
proposals.evidence: Simonsohn, Simmons & Nelson, Nature Human Behaviour 2020 https://www.nature.com/articles/s41562-020-0912-z ; Comet toolbox for network neuroscience multiverse https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12892349/ ; multiverse visualisation at scale https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12875576/ ; Gelman on spec curves https://statmodeling.stat.columbia.edu/2024/11/12/specification-curve-analysis-and-the-multiverse/ ; project ordering defect: memory/new_repo_rebuild_aug2026.md defect #6

proposals.title: Name the hierarchy: session is the random effect; subject is NEVER a random effect at k<=5
proposals.detail: Replace 'a mixed-effects or cluster-robust method is required wherever n_units >> n_sessions >> n_subjects' with an explicit hierarchy (trial < unit < session < subject) and explicit rules: session-level random intercept is the default random effect (n = 25-45 per subject, adequate); subject enters as a FIXED effect or by per-subject stratification, never as a random effect while k <= 5, because a 3-level variance component is unestimable and will converge to ~0 and hand back pooled inference. Require the mixedlm and a cluster-robust OLS to be fitted as a pair with the convergence flag recorded, preferring the cluster-robust fit when the flag fires. Name the hierarchical bootstrap as the sanctioned alternative when the claim aggregates units within sessions within subjects and the response is not plausibly linear-Gaussian.
proposals.rationale: As written the gate is satisfiable by `groups=subject` at k=3, which produces a false sense of rigor — the model is pooled inference with extra steps. The lab's own battery already prescribes the mixedlm/cluster-robust pair with a convergence flag because statsmodels silently fails to converge at near-zero RE variance; that operational detail must live in the ADR, not only in a prose skill. Traditional independence-assuming tests on nested neural data show false-positive rates over 45% at a nominal 5%, so getting the level right is not a nicety.
proposals.evidence: e:/python_analysis/git_repos/vis_detect_analysis_Sep2025/.claude/skills/harden-result/SKILL.md Gate 3 (mixedlm + cluster-robust pair, convergence flag, per-session sign test); Saravanan, Berman & Sober hierarchical bootstrap https://www.biorxiv.org/content/10.1101/819334v2.full and https://arxiv.org/pdf/2007.07797 ; master design ADR-010 table row 'Pseudoreplication declaration'

proposals.title: Per-subject and per-region estimate array + explicit scope-of-inference are required fields, gated on `confirmed`
proposals.detail: Add three fields to every ledger row: `per_subject` (an array of subject -> estimate + CI, one entry per subject contributing), `n_subjects_replicating` (k of N with same-sign effect), and `scope_of_inference` (a one-line string chosen from a controlled vocabulary: single-subject observation / within-subject effect replicated in k of N subjects / cross-subject generalisation). A gate blocks promotion to `confirmed` when `per_subject` is missing or when the effect reverses sign in any subject without that being stated in the claim. The claim's wording must be derivable from `scope_of_inference` — 'striatal neurons do X' is not writable from a row whose scope is single-subject.
proposals.rationale: With 1-3 subjects driving most claims, subject-level generalisation is formally impossible and the honest standard is per-subject replication reported as such, matching journal reporting checklists that demand n be defined as 'x cells from x animals'. This project has already been burned in both directions by pooling: BG_046 rho = +0.20 and BG_031 rho = -0.10 cancelled into a fake pooled null, and a region-composition difference has masqueraded as an effect. A structured field makes that mechanically checkable instead of a habit.
proposals.evidence: e:/python_analysis/git_repos/vis_detect_analysis_Sep2025/.claude/skills/harden-result/SKILL.md Gate 4 (Simpson's paradox in both directions, measured); Nature Neuroscience reporting checklist on defining n and biological replication https://pure.mpg.de/rest/items/item_2328407_6/component/file_2398069/content ; eNeuro 2026 on experimental-unit misidentification inflating n https://www.eneuro.org/content/13/2/ENEURO.0007-26.2026

proposals.title: Add `inconclusive` status and require TOST/equivalence for any claim reported as a null
proposals.detail: Extend the Status vocabulary to `exploratory` / `confirmed` / `inconclusive` / `retracted` / `refuted`, and require that any row whose claim is a negative result carries an equivalence test (TOST, or the CI-vs-bound form) against the pre-registered minimum interesting effect from ADR-010. A negative that rejects effects larger than the MIE is a `null` result and can be claimed as one; a negative that does not is `inconclusive` and must be worded as underpowered. Store the equivalence bound and the observed CI in the row so a reader can see what was excluded.
proposals.rationale: This project's most valuable outputs to date are honest negatives — the leakage-controlled within-FA timing null, the single-cell TF-encoding null across three mice, and the post-normalisation null that forced a retraction — and the ledger currently has no way to distinguish 'we can exclude anything bigger than d = 0.2' from 'we had no power'. Since ADR-010 already forces a minimum interesting effect to be pre-registered, the equivalence bound is free: it is that number. Without this, every null in the ledger reads as equally weak, which undersells the good ones and oversells the thin ones.
proposals.evidence: Lakens, Equivalence Tests: A Practical Primer https://journals.sagepub.com/doi/full/10.1177/1948550617697177 ; Lakens, Scheel & Isager tutorial https://journals.sagepub.com/doi/10.1177/2515245918770963 ; project nulls: memory notes n1_neural_phase_jun2026 and state_tf_encoding_population_geometry_jul2026

proposals.title: Split into parameter recovery AND model recovery; require recovery at realistic n and stimulus statistics
proposals.detail: Requirement 2 currently reads 'every new estimator demonstrates parameter recovery'. Split it: (2a) parameter recovery for every estimator, reported as a simulated-vs-recovered scatter per parameter, not a single correlation coefficient; (2b) model recovery — a confusion matrix from simulating under each candidate model and fitting all of them — required wherever a claim rests on model comparison or on a selected model order. That covers the three places this project's headlines actually live: DDM variant selection (learning changes drift vs threshold vs start-point), GLM-HMM state count K, and the number of retained population dimensions. Recovery must be run at the trial counts, change-size distribution and firing rates of real sessions, because DDM drift/boundary collinearity and HMM state identifiability are strongly n-dependent.
proposals.rationale: Parameter recovery says an estimator can find its own parameters; it says nothing about whether the data can distinguish the model whose parameters they are. 'Learning raises drift rather than threshold' is a model-comparison claim and is exactly the sort that survives parameter recovery and fails model recovery. The field-standard triad for these estimator classes is parameter recovery, model recovery, and posterior predictive check, and the GLM-HMM lineage this project follows did exactly that (generative-parameter recovery plus cross-validated model comparison plus posterior state probabilities).
proposals.evidence: Wilson & Collins, eLife 2019, Ten simple rules for the computational modeling of behavioral data https://elifesciences.org/articles/49547 (parameter recovery: plot simulated vs recovered, do not rely on r; model recovery: confusion matrix); Ashwood et al., Nat Neurosci 2022 https://www.nature.com/articles/s41593-021-01007-z ; project estimators: src/visdetect/analysis/ddm.py, hmm.py, tf_glm.py, decision_latents*.py

proposals.title: Let the recovery run set the minimum interesting effect, so MIE stops being arbitrary
proposals.detail: Require every synthetic recovery run to emit one extra number: the estimator's resolution floor at realistic n — the smallest ground-truth effect the estimator recovers with, say, 80% sign-consistency and CI excluding zero. Store it in the same artefact as the recovery result, and have ADR-010's pre-specification template read the MIE field from it by default, with any smaller MIE requiring an explicit written override. For the TF-GLM kernel-width estimator specifically, run the recovery across a grid of ground-truth firing rates and require the width estimate to be FR-invariant.
proposals.rationale: The MIE field is the weakest link in the pre-specification row because researchers have no principled way to pick it and will pick whatever makes the result interesting. Grounding it in the estimator's own resolution makes it defensible, non-negotiable, and computed before anyone has seen the answer. The FR-grid clause targets the project's single most expensive failure directly: the retracted transient/sustained result was a raw-Hz artifact in a cross-neuron magnitude comparison, and an FR-swept recovery would have exposed the estimator's FR dependence at the moment it was written rather than after it produced a finding.
proposals.evidence: master design ADR-014 rationale ('recovery would have caught the circularity bug at the moment the estimator was written'); harden-result SKILL.md Gate 1 and the 2026-07-02 retraction (raw Hz, p = 4.9e-3 -> FR-normalised p = 0.37); src/visdetect/utils/synthetic.py (currently incidental, ADR-014 makes it load-bearing)

proposals.title: Specify the null: dependency-respecting shuffle, quantitative flatness criterion, permutation-count floor
proposals.detail: 'Its recorded output must be flat' is not checkable. Require each null to record: (i) the surrogate type and the level at which randomisation occurs — within-session trial-label shuffle, circular shift for time series, session-block shuffle for cross-session claims; a global shuffle that destroys the dependency structure is anti-conservative and must fail the gate; (ii) a quantitative flatness criterion — the null's central tendency within a stated tolerance of theoretical chance (decoder null mean vs 0.5) and the observed statistic's percentile in the null; (iii) the number of permutations, with a hard rule that no reported permutation p may be smaller than 1/(n_perm + 1). Scope the requirement to analyses that produce an inferential statistic entering the ledger; descriptive and QC artefacts are exempt but must be labelled descriptive.
proposals.rationale: As written the gate can be satisfied by a shuffle that is both wrong and reassuring — shuffling labels across sessions when the claim is cross-session manufactures a null that is far too narrow, which makes almost anything significant. The p-floor rule matters here because the project's conventions specify 200-1000 shuffles while its write-ups quote p < 0.001. Scoping to inferential outputs is what stops the gate from being bypassed wholesale: a null control for a raster or a psychometric curve is meaningless, and an over-broad gate is the kind researchers learn to route around.
proposals.evidence: master design ADR-014 requirement 1; CLAUDE.md conventions (permutation tests 500-1000 shuffles; decoder null 'chance as mean +/- 2 SD of null' over >= 200 shuffles); harden-result SKILL.md Gate 2 held-out-sign control as the template for a dependency-respecting surrogate

proposals.title: Randomness is provenance: record seed policy, resample counts, and resampling unit in the sidecar
proposals.detail: S5's five parts (execution log, code, environment, inputs, git sha) omit everything stochastic. Add a sixth: the RNG record — the seed or seed sequence actually used, n_permutations, n_bootstrap, and the resampling unit (trial / unit / session / subject). Replace the global `seed=42` convention with a registered helper `rng_for(analysis_id, purpose)` in the must-import registry, deriving an independent stream per analysis and per purpose from a recorded root, so a split-half stability check is not silently sharing randomness with the primary fit and so seed-shopping leaves a trace. Require the bootstrap's resampling unit to be declared in the same place as the pseudoreplication declaration, and forbid bootstrapping over subjects at k <= 5.
proposals.rationale: A fixed global seed makes a run reproducible but makes independent checks non-independent, and a percentile bootstrap over the wrong level is the pseudoreplication bug in bootstrap clothing — resampling trials when the replicate is the session is precisely how B10's 'VMS engagement-gated tracking' survived until CIs were bootstrapped over sessions. Recording the resampling unit next to the estimate makes that class of error visible in the artefact rather than discoverable only by reading the script.
proposals.evidence: master design S5; CLAUDE.md statistical standards ('Bootstrap CI, 1000 resamples, seed=42, percentile method'); harden-result SKILL.md Gate 3 (B10 collapse once CIs bootstrapped over sessions rather than trials)

proposals.title: `prespec_sha` field with a mechanical ancestry/timestamp check
proposals.detail: ADR-010 requires the pre-specification to be committed before the analysis runs, but nothing binds a ledger row to that commit. Add a required `prespec_sha` field, and a gate that verifies the pre-spec commit is an ancestor of the analysis commit and strictly earlier in time. A claim whose `prespec_sha` fails the check, or is absent, is capped at `exploratory` no matter how small its p-value; only pre-specified claims are eligible for `confirmed`. This is the only place in the design where pre-registration is currently a norm rather than a check.
proposals.rationale: Timestamped pre-registration at zero cost is the design's best statistical idea, and it is exactly the kind of norm that erodes first, because writing the prediction after seeing the result is invisible to every other gate. Binding it to a verifiable commit ancestry applies ADR-003's own philosophy — anything mechanically checkable becomes a build-breaking gate — to the statistical layer, and it gives the ledger a hard, auditable line between confirmatory and exploratory that a reader outside the project can verify.
proposals.evidence: master design ADR-010 row 'Pre-specification' and ADR-003 ('anything mechanically checkable becomes a build-breaking gate'); ADR-012's stated reliance on pre-specification as one of only two mitigations for forking paths

proposals.title: Add trial-count matching and composition/yield-bias control to the required verification battery
proposals.detail: The Verification field enumerates FR-normalisation, circularity, pseudoreplication, per-region breakdown and leakage controls, and omits two confounds this project has already measured. Add (i) trial-count matching for any comparison of encoding strength, fit quality or selectivity between conditions, since fit-quality metrics are trial-count attenuated and an under-sampled condition manufactures a difference; and (ii) a composition/yield-bias control for any cross-stage or cross-region cell-type claim — rate-matched resampling or composition as an explicit covariate — with the caveat written into the stats sidecar beside the number.
proposals.rationale: Both are live, quantified threats to the paper's actual headline. Encoding-strength attenuation already produced an apparent state difference that was power, not biology. Yield bias is larger still for a learning paper: FSI fraction runs 84% / 71% / 43% across subjects against a true composition near 90-95% SPN, and chronic drift moves broad/SPN share from 89% to 15% across stages — so any cross-stage cell-type comparison is confounded by construction unless composition is controlled. A verification list that omits the confound most likely to break the headline is incomplete.
proposals.evidence: e:/python_analysis/git_repos/vis_detect_analysis_Sep2025/.claude/skills/harden-result/SKILL.md Gates 5 and 7 (B9 trial-count attenuation; FSI:SPN yield figures; 89% -> 15% drift); memory/qc_celltype_yield_investigation_jun2026

proposals.title: Promote the verification battery from prose skill to `visdetect.verify`, landed in sub-project 2 not 5
proposals.detail: The lab's eight-gate hardening battery currently exists only as a prose skill in the AI layer, which the build order schedules last (sub-project 5) — meaning the entire analysis port in sub-project 3 runs without the project's strongest scientific instrument available. Reimplement it as a library module (`fr_normalisation_check`, `session_re_and_cluster_robust`, `per_subject_breakdown`, `trial_count_match`, `leakage_cascade`, `composition_control`), each returning a structured record, and land it with the enforcement gates in sub-project 2. ADR-013's Verification field is then generated from those records rather than typed as free text, and the prose skill becomes a thin pointer to the module.
proposals.rationale: The design's own argument for ADR-005 — that a hand-maintained factual document goes stale and a stale instruction actively misleads every future session — applies with equal force to a prose statistics battery, and it has already happened: the current skill hardcodes an Opus 4.8 requirement against the user's standing Opus 5 rule. A free-text 'which battery was applied' field will rot the same way. Structured records also make the battery auditable across the ledger: you can ask which claims never ran a leakage control.
proposals.evidence: e:/python_analysis/git_repos/vis_detect_analysis_Sep2025/.claude/skills/harden-result/SKILL.md (296 lines of prose; Gate 8 hardcodes 'claude-opus-4-8'); master design section 7 build order (AI layer = sub-project 5, analysis port = sub-project 3); ADR-005 rationale on generated-not-copied factual content

proposals.title: A sanctioned parameter-override mechanism, restricted to the sensitivity harness
proposals.detail: S1 forces every threshold to have exactly one definition and bans inline magic numbers, which is correct — and which, without an escape hatch, makes a QC-threshold sweep either impossible or a reason to bypass the registry. Specify a single sanctioned mechanism: a frozen constants object with a context-managed override (`with constants.override(min_fr=0.5): ...`) that is importable only from the declared sensitivity-sweep harness and from tests, banned everywhere else by the same AST gate that bans shadow definitions, and whose active overrides are written into the provenance sidecar of any artefact produced under it.
proposals.rationale: Without this, the two halves of the design fight: ADR-003 wants one definition, and robustness analysis needs many. The consequence of not resolving it is predictable from the old repo — people retype the literal locally, which is the exact pathology being cured (four disagreeing firing-rate floors, canonical DEFAULT_MIN_FR dead code). Recording active overrides in the sidecar also means a sweep artefact can never be mistaken for a default-parameter artefact.
proposals.evidence: master design S1 and ADR-003; memory/new_repo_rebuild_aug2026.md defects #2 (load_qc_profile returns {} so strict and lenient are byte-identical) and #8 (four disagreeing firing-rate floors) — the project currently cannot state how sensitive its unit counts are to QC profile

proposals.title: Split-half / interleaved stability as a cheap standing robustness column
proposals.detail: Require every claim entering the ledger to report one stability number: the effect re-estimated on interleaved halves (odd vs even sessions for cross-session claims; odd vs even trials for within-session claims), with both point estimates and their agreement. Store as a `stability` field. Use interleaved, never chronological, halves for this project, because a first-half/second-half split is confounded with the learning axis that most claims are about.
proposals.rationale: This is the cheapest available protection against overfitting to a particular subset and costs one extra function call on already-cached data. It is not a confirmatory cohort and reserves nothing, so it does not touch the settled ADR-012 deferral. It complements the specification curve: the curve tests robustness to analytic choices, split-half tests robustness to which data you happened to look at.
proposals.evidence: master design ADR-012 (settled: no data reserved; within-analysis holdout used wherever supported); memory/session_grouping_learning_axis_jul2026 (chronological splits are entangled with the learning axis, so interleaving is required)

proposals.target: NEW-ADR (design sensitivity), feeding ADR-012's revisit trigger
proposals.title: Simulation-based design sensitivity: what effect is detectable at k subjects
proposals.detail: Add a small design-sensitivity module that resamples the existing BG_046/BG_031/BG_039 sessions to answer, for each primary claim class, what effect magnitude is detectable at k subjects x n sessions under the session-clustered inference the pseudoreplication gate mandates. Report the detectable-effect curve as a function of subject count. The output is a decision input for how many more mice the paper needs, and it is the natural evidence base for the ADR-012 revisit trigger, which currently fires on the qualitative condition 'when subject count and quality support it'.
proposals.rationale: The project is actively acquiring more subjects and has no quantitative basis for how many are enough, or for what the confirmatory-cohort deferral would cost in power if reversed. Because the data already exist, this is a resampling exercise rather than a real power calculation, so it is affordable and honest, and it converts the ADR-012 revisit trigger from a judgement call into a threshold. It also feeds back into the MIE field: if the detectable effect at k = 3 exceeds a claim's stated MIE, the claim is not testable at current n and should be declared so up front.
proposals.evidence: master design ADR-012 ('revisit when the additional experiments currently in progress land and subject count and quality support it') — no quantitative criterion is given; simulation-based power for the smallest effect size of interest https://www.researchgate.net/publication/378611133_Simulation-Based_Power_Analyses_for_the_Smallest_Effect_Size_of_Interest_A_Confidence_Interval_Approach_for_Minimum-Effect_and_Equivalence_Testing

proposals.target: ADR-013 (Effect size + CI field) — with a new `visdetect.stats.effects` module in ADR-010's must-import registry
proposals.title: Name the canonical effect size per test class and require it computed at the inference level
proposals.detail: 'Effect size + CI' is required but unspecified, which invites a Cohen's d on raw Hz — the exact shape of the retracted result. Fix the mapping in one module registered in the must-import list: rank-biserial correlation for Mann-Whitney, Spearman rho with CI via Fisher-z computed on session-level values, Cohen's d only on normalised quantities, chance-corrected AUC for decoders with the permutation null as its reference, and an explicit ban on quoting Delta-AIC/Delta-BIC as an effect size. Add the rule that the effect size must be computed at the same level as the inference: a session-clustered test reports a session-level effect size, not a cell-session-level one.
proposals.rationale: Mismatched levels are how a pooled cell-session effect size gets attached to a session-clustered p-value and reads as far stronger than the evidence supports. A single registered module also closes the same-name-different-behaviour class that ADR-010 already identifies as the most severe duplication failure — partial_spearman exists in three mathematically different forms in the old repo and underpins two live claims. The Delta-BIC ban is not generic: a Delta-BIC of +242 in this project fired on right-skew alone and collapsed to +2.4 after log transform.
proposals.evidence: master design ADR-010 ('same name, different behaviour' fails hardest; partial_spearman in three forms); harden-result SKILL.md red-flag table (GMM Delta-BIC = +242 -> +2.4 after log transform); CLAUDE.md 'Report effect sizes alongside every p-value'

overbuilt: ADR-014's 'every analysis ships a null control' applied literally to every analysis. A null control for a psychometric curve, a raster, or a QC yield plot is meaningless, and an over-broad gate is the kind people learn to route around — which then kills it for the analyses that need it. Simplification: scope the requirement to analyses producing an inferential statistic that enters the ledger; descriptive and QC artefacts are exempt but must be labelled descriptive.

ADR-014's 'where the null is cheap it runs in CI'. The repo will not have the 30 GB of pkls available to CI, so a real-data null cannot run there under any budget. Simplification: CI runs synthetic-data null smoke tests only (does the null harness produce a flat distribution on data with no injected effect); real-data nulls use the design's own better mechanism — stored result, currency check against the analysis code, quantitative flatness criterion.

ADR-013's Verification field as free text ('which battery was applied'). At ledger scale this becomes an unverifiable string that drifts from what actually ran, reproducing in miniature the CLAUDE.md-vs-constants.py problem the whole rebuild exists to fix. Simplification: generate it from the structured records returned by the `visdetect.verify` module rather than typing it.

Requiring a specification curve for every claim would be a genuine tax on exploration at this scale. Keep it strictly scoped to rows promoted to `confirmed`, with exploratory rows explicitly exempt — the curve is an admission-to-headline cost, not a working cost.

The ADR-012 mechanism (cohort field + loader guard) is right to build and defer, but resist adding further per-row cohort bookkeeping until it is activated. While every session is `discovery`, the field is a one-value column and any gate reasoning over it is dead weight.
open_questions: What is the reviewable unit for a specification curve when the headline rests on a per-unit GLM refit? A full factorial over QC threshold and unit selection means refitting thousands of kernels per spec. Is a coarse 3-point sweep on refit-requiring axes plus a full factorial on post-hoc axes acceptable, or does the joint inference need the complete grid to be valid?

Does the project want the session-ordering axis (calendar date / trials completed / d-prime stage / blinded-sorter label) treated as a multiverse degree of freedom, or as a single decision to be settled once in the decision log under ADR-011? These have different consequences: the former reports learning slopes as a distribution, the latter picks one and defends it.

For DDM fits, is the inference target per-session parameters (n = 25-45 per subject, session as the replicate) or a hierarchical fit pooling sessions within subject? The choice determines whether the pseudoreplication gate applies to the DDM at all, and whether parameter recovery must be run at per-session or per-subject trial counts.

Should a claim that holds in one subject and reverses in another be recordable as `confirmed` with a scoped claim string, or forced to `exploratory`? The design needs one answer, because the project has at least one measured instance (rho = +0.20 vs -0.10) and the honest wording depends on which rule is in force.

Who arbitrates the minimum interesting effect when the recovery-derived resolution floor exceeds the biologically meaningful effect — i.e. when the estimator cannot resolve what matters? Options are declaring the question untestable at current n, redesigning the estimator, or feeding it to the design-sensitivity module as a subject-count requirement.

Is there appetite for a lightweight external check on `confirmed` rows — a second reader, or a public preprint of the pre-specification — given that within a solo lab the pre-spec commit is authored by the same person who later interprets the result? The commit-ancestry gate proves ordering, not independence.

reports.lens: Reproducibility engineering (research software engineering: environment pinning, numerical determinism, data versioning, CI topology, backup)
reports.overall_verdict: On provenance this design is well ahead of typical systems-neuroscience practice — S5's five-part sidecar with the execution log as authority, ADR-011's append-only decision log for session inclusion, and ADR-014's synthetic-recovery gate are things most labs (and most published papers) simply do not have. But there is a structural hole running through it: the design consistently RECORDS state and never PINS it. S5 records "environment (language + every package version)"; no ADR produces a lockfile, sets a Python version policy, or controls BLAS threading. ADR-009 makes `unexplained` the only failing verdict but Open Question 4 defers the tolerance that decides what "a difference" even is — so the gate as written fires on the last ULP. ADR-008 delegates off-disk safety to "the remote", but the remote is git and every byte that matters (30 GB pkls, 16 GB caches, the registry, the hand-labels) is gitignored, so the real state is 1 copy / 1 medium / 0 offsite. And the gates have no runner: 30 of 104 test files need real data that lives on one Windows box, with no fixture small enough to run in cloud CI. The environment domain has already reproduced the exact defect class the rebuild exists to kill — `setup.cfg` carries zero version bounds, `environment.yml` pins `numpy<2`, and the live `.venv` runs numpy 2.2.6. Five new or modified ADRs close this; nothing in the existing fourteen needs to be reversed.
matches_best_practice: S5's execution-log-authoritative provenance exceeds field norm. The standard failure is exactly what the recon measured — zero git sha across 3,056 figures — and most labs' remedy is a git sha in the filename, which records the code that *should* have run. Making the log authoritative over the recorded code is the right and unusual call.

Build order putting enforcement (sub-project 2) before the analysis port (3) is correct and rarely done. Gates written after the code they govern get bent to fit it; this is the highest-leverage sequencing decision in the document.

ADR-005 (generated CLAUDE.md, CI fails on regeneration diff) is the standard technique for killing doc rot, correctly applied to an AI instruction file. ADR-010's mitigation — template generated from the same source as the gates — closes the obvious second-order drift.

ADR-002 + S8 (analysis installs without the UnitMatch/GPU/MATLAB stack, verified by a clean-env install) is what makes the analysis layer independently reproducible. It is also what makes the uv/pixi split in proposal 1 viable, since the pure-PyPI half is the half that produces figures.

ADR-011's append-only, attributed decision log for session inclusion/exclusion is the data-side equivalent of pre-registration and is ahead of the field. The `.bak` evidence (BG_031 silently losing `19052025`) is a textbook justification.

ADR-014's synthetic parameter recovery as a *gate* rather than a habit. Recovery-on-ground-truth is standard inside modelling papers and almost never enforced in CI; making `utils/synthetic.py` load-bearing is also what unlocks hermetic cloud CI (proposal 5).
ADR-008's no-junctions rule is a correct, permanent, structural fix to a measured data-loss class — it removes the capability rather than adding a warning.

ADR-013's ledger with a mandatory `retracted`/`refuted` status and required effect size + CI. At n = thousands of units a p-value-only row is actively misleading, and a visible retraction record is a reproducibility artefact in its own right.

proposals.target: NEW-ADR (ADR-015) — Environment is pinned by a committed lockfile, not merely recorded
proposals.title: uv.lock for the analysis stack, pixi.lock for the heavy stack, Python 3.12 floor; S5 records the lockfile hash
proposals.detail: Adopt `uv` as the environment manager for the foundation + analysis layers, with a single universal `uv.lock` covering `win_amd64` and `linux_x86_64` in one file, committed to git; export `pylock.toml` (PEP 751, Final 2025-03-31) as the tool-neutral artefact that S5's environment field references by hash. The whole analysis dependency set is pure-PyPI with wheels (numpy, scipy, pandas, matplotlib, seaborn, sklearn, h5py, pyddm, brainglobe-atlasapi), so uv is sufficient and pixi's conda-forge machinery is unnecessary there. Keep the heavy layer (Kilosort4/CUDA, UnitMatchPy, mtscomp, DANT) in a separate `pixi.toml`/`pixi.lock`, which genuinely needs conda-forge native libraries — and per S8 that environment is never required to reproduce a figure. Set `requires-python = ">=3.12"`: 3.10 (what `.venv` runs today) is security-only and reaches EOL in October 2026. Amend S5 so "environment" means lockfile hash + resolved Python version + platform tag, not a `pip freeze` dump.
proposals.rationale: The environment domain has already reproduced the rebuild's headline defect — one definition in three places, silently divergent. Measured now: `setup.cfg` install_requires has zero version bounds; `environment.yml` pins `numpy<2`; the live `.venv` runs numpy 2.2.6. numpy 1→2 changed integer promotion and removed public aliases, so `pip install -e .` and `conda env create -f environment.yml` today produce environments that can compute different numbers. No ADR covers this and no gate detects it; S5 as written would faithfully record the divergence in every sidecar without ever preventing it. Recording an unpinned environment does not make a result reproducible, it makes the irreproducibility auditable after the fact.
proposals.evidence: Measured in-repo: e:/python_analysis/git_repos/vis_detect_analysis_Sep2025/setup.cfg (install_requires, no bounds) vs environment.yml (`numpy<2`) vs `.venv/Scripts/python.exe -c "import numpy; print(numpy.__version__)"` -> 2.2.6, Python 3.10.9. Tool choice: https://pydevtools.com/handbook/explanation/uv-vs-pixi-vs-conda-for-scientific-python/ (uv when deps are PyPI-with-wheels; pixi when native/CUDA libs are needed; conda's environment.yml "is a specification, not a lock"). Lockfile standard: https://peps.python.org/pep-0751/ (pylock.toml, Final 2025-03-31; hashes mandatory; one file covers multiple platforms via environment markers). Python EOL: https://devguide.python.org/versions/ (3.10 security-only, EOL Oct 2026; 3.12 bugfix to Oct 2028).

proposals.target: NEW-ADR (ADR-016) — Determinism policy: generator-passing, thread pinning, tolerance-based comparison
proposals.title: Ban the global RNG and the seed literal; pin BLAS threads; make tolerance a first-class attribution, not Open Question 4
proposals.detail: Three mandates, all gate-enforceable in sub-project 2. (a) Generator-passing, entropy-recorded: an AST gate bans `np.random.seed` and bare `np.random.*` draws in library and script code; every stochastic function takes an explicit `rng: np.random.Generator`; entry points build one via `np.random.default_rng(entropy)` where `entropy` is a 128-bit value generated per run and written into the provenance sidecar, with `rng.spawn(n)` for parallel workers. Explicitly REJECT a seed registry — registering 20 magic numbers re-creates the shadow-constant pathology in a new costume; what gets registered is entropy per RUN, in the log, not literals per CALL SITE, in the code. (b) Thread pinning: worker entry points wrap compute in `threadpoolctl.threadpool_limits(1)` and the sidecar records resolved BLAS name, version and thread count. (c) Tolerance: add a fifth ADR-009 attribution, `numerical-noise`, defined by a measured per-analysis-class floor — run the component 5x on the same input across both platforms and both thread settings, take the observed spread, and treat differences inside it as noise. Outside it, `unexplained` still blocks.
proposals.rationale: ADR-009 makes `unexplained` the only failing verdict, but Open Question 4 defers the tolerance to the specs — so the gate currently has no noise floor and every last-bit float difference is a blocking failure. That is not a deferrable detail, it is the definition of the gate's failing condition. Bit-identity across laptop and HPC is also unattainable here by construction: this numpy ships scipy-openblas 0.3.29 built DYNAMIC_ARCH with MAX_THREADS=24, so the kernel is selected from the runtime CPU and reduction order changes with thread count — floating-point addition is non-associative, so the sum changes. Spending port effort chasing bit-identity would fail for reasons unrelated to the port. On seeding, the codebase is already 80 files on `default_rng` against only 3 using `np.random.seed`, so the ban is cheap now and expensive later.
proposals.evidence: Measured: `numpy.show_config()` in the project venv -> `openblas configuration: OpenBLAS 0.3.29 USE64BITINT DYNAMIC_ARCH NO_AFFINITY Haswell MAX_THREADS=24`. Seed inventory over src+scripts+tests: 396 seed-literal matches, 35 distinct values (0,1,2,...,42,55,99,111,123,12345,20260621); 3 files use `np.random.seed`, 80 use `default_rng`; only 10 files touch OMP/MKL/threadpool env at all. Non-associativity + thread count as the mechanism, and the CNR fixed-thread remedy: https://www.intel.com/content/www/us/en/developer/archive/training/conditional-numerical-reproducibility-cnr.html. RNG discipline (pass Generators, avoid global state, `spawn` for parallel, no bitstream guarantee across numpy versions — which is why (a) needs ADR-015): https://blog.scientific-python.org/numpy/numpy-rng/ and https://numpy.org/doc/stable/reference/random/bit_generators/generated/numpy.random.SeedSequence.html

proposals.target: ADR-008 ("Off-disk safety is the remote's job") + NEW success criterion for backup
proposals.title: The remote holds none of the data; state a 3-2-1 policy for non-git artefacts and make the hash manifest the verification mechanism
proposals.detail: ADR-008 rejects a second drive on the grounds that off-disk safety is the remote's job. That is true for code and false for everything else: `.gitignore` excludes `data/`, `FIGURES/`, `*.pkl`, `data/cache/*`, so the git remote holds none of the 30.5 GB of pkls, 15.9 GB of caches, 36.1 GB of figures, the registry, or the hand-labels.
