Replace the sentence with a policy: (i) the four irreplaceable hand-made files (~27 KB — 217 hand-drawn state episodes, 133 blinded session sorts, the state rule + pkl, pupil sidecars) go into git via `git add -f`, since they are text-sized and no rerun regenerates them; (ii) registry + decision log + hash manifest sync daily to institutional storage via `rclone sync --checksum`; (iii) derived caches and figures sync weekly; (iv) a quarterly RESTORE TEST pulls a random artefact and verifies its BLAKE3 against the manifest from proposal 5. Note explicitly that rclone to institutional storage is I/O, not compute, so it is a documented exception to the no-work-over-Samba rule, scheduled off-hours.
proposals.rationale: Sub-project -1 was a one-time rescue of COMMITS, and it worked. It did not create a policy, and the hand-label copy it produced went to `e:\python_analysis\_handlabel_backup_20260806` — the same physical disk, which the memory note itself flags as accidental-deletion protection only, not disk-failure protection. So the steady state for everything non-git is one copy, one medium, zero offsite. A rebuild whose entire premise is that results must be reproducible cannot leave the only copy of the roster, the registry and the irreplaceable hand-labels on one E: drive; a disk failure invalidates every ledger row that cites them. This is also the cheapest proposal in the set — the hand-labels are 27 KB.
proposals.evidence: Repo `.gitignore`: `*.pkl`, `data/`, `data/cache/*`, `FIGURES/`, `figs/`, `table_output/`. Sizes from audit spec D4: 285 pkls / 30.5 GB, 16,779 cache files / 15.9 GB, 3,056 figures / 36.1 GB. Same-disk backup admission: memory/new_repo_rebuild_aug2026.md ("Only copy off the repo tree is `e:\python_analysis\_handlabel_backup_20260806`, same physical disk") and audit spec §8 "Still open". 3-2-1 with mandatory checksum verification and scheduled restore tests: https://www.avepoint.com/blog/backup/what-is-the-3-2-1-backup-rule ; rclone as sync/verify mechanism: https://dohost.us/index.php/2026/03/31/automation-with-rclone-scripting-your-3-2-1-offsite-transfers/

proposals.target: ADR-003 (gate list) + sub-project 2 spec — CI topology
proposals.title: Four-tier CI with a committed golden mini-session; local full-data tier verified by a commit-pinned receipt; NO self-hosted runner on the data box
proposals.detail: Specify the runner topology the gates depend on. Tier 0 (hermetic, GitHub-hosted, win+linux matrix): AST gates, import-contract check, ADR-005 doc-regeneration diff, `uv lock --check`, tests on `utils/synthetic.py` sessions. Tier 1 — the missing piece — a committed GOLDEN MINI-SESSION: decimate one real session to ~20 units x ~200 trials with all outcome classes plus a suffixed twin and a day-1-9 date represented (a few MB), commit it, and run alignment / EVENT_VALID_OUTCOMES / SDT / normalization / registry-identity tests against it in cloud CI. Tier 2 (full data, local): `nox -s fulldata` on the Windows box writes `.ci/receipts/fulldata-<sha>.json` recording commit sha + lockfile hash + a results digest; a Tier-0 job FAILS THE MERGE if no receipt matches HEAD. Tier 3 (nightly/HPC): expensive ADR-014 nulls as a Slurm job committing a status file. Explicitly rule out a self-hosted runner on the workstation.
proposals.rationale: ADR-003 makes gates the load-bearing mechanism of the whole design but never says where they execute, and 30 of the current repo's 104 test files touch real sessions that exist only on one Windows box. Without Tier 1 the gates either run on nothing real or do not run at all — which is how the current repo arrived at zero CI. The insight is that almost none of those 30 tests need 30 GB; they need a session of realistic SHAPE, and a committed mini-session converts most of them into cloud-runnable checks. The receipt pattern makes "required local hook" verifiable rather than honour-system, because the receipt is pinned to a commit sha and a stale local run cannot pass. The self-hosted runner is the obvious alternative and should be refused: the project treats this repo as public-facing, and GitHub is explicit that fork pull requests can execute arbitrary code on a self-hosted machine — which here is the machine holding the only copy of the data.
proposals.evidence: Measured: `find tests -name '*.py' | wc -l` -> 104; `grep -rlE 'load_session|\.pkl|load_staging_manifest|PKL_DIR|data/cache' tests/` -> 30 files. Zero CI confirmed in audit spec D5 and memory note ("zero CI, zero linters, zero pre-commit... only automated gate is guard_recursive_delete.ps1"). Public-facing convention: memory/feedback_no_full_name_in_artifacts. GitHub guidance: https://docs.github.com/en/actions/how-tos/manage-runners/self-hosted-runners/manage-access — "We recommend that you only use self-hosted runners with private repositories."

proposals.target: ADR-004 / ADR-011 — data versioning mechanism (resolves Open Question 3)
proposals.title: Commit a manifest-of-hashes; reject DVC / DataLad / git-annex at this scale and record why
proposals.detail: Make the answer explicit rather than leaving it to Open Question 3. The registry already hashes inputs (ADR-004); commit that as `registry/session-manifest.tsv` — a few hundred rows, tens of KB — with columns `session_key, path, size, mtime_ns, blake3, ingest_code_sha, first_seen_commit, regenerable{yes|no}`. Verification is two-speed: fast (size + mtime_ns) on every run, full BLAKE3 on ingest and in the nightly job. The `regenerable` column matters: pkls are DERIVED from raw SpikeGLX on institutional storage, so recording the ingest recipe (code sha + params) makes them reproducible rather than precious, while the ~27 KB of hand-made files are `regenerable=no` and go into git. Decline DVC, DataLad and git-annex for v1 in writing, so the decision is not revisited every six months.
proposals.rationale: DVC/DataLad buy branch-switchable data, dataset nesting, and multi-site distribution. This project is one user, one box, one branch of data, and cannot use any of the three; what it gets instead is a second add/push discipline, a second remote to host, and a failure mode (a data checkout silently disagreeing with the code checkout) harder to debug than the problem it solves. DataLad is the honest alternative — neuroscience-native, git-annex-backed — but its value arrives at PUBLICATION time when the dataset is shared, a later and separable decision. The measured failure here was never "we lost a version of a pkl"; it was 15,802 corrupted session-id rows and a roster mutated in place with no record. A hash manifest plus ADR-011's decision log addresses both and costs one generated file. DVC also changed ownership in November 2025, a further argument against betting a solo project's data layer on it now.
proposals.evidence: Scale from audit spec D4: 285 pkls / 30.5 GB, 327 CSVs carrying a session-id column. DataLad/DVC architecture comparison ("Git only tracks information on where this data can be found"; DVC targets ML practitioners, DataLad targets researchers): https://handbook.datalad.org/en/latest/beyond_basics/101-168-dvc.html and https://openneuroscience.org/Resources/DataLad. DVC ownership change: https://lakefs.io/data-version-control/dvc-tools/. Motivating defects: memory/new_repo_rebuild_aug2026.md items 1 and 3.

proposals.target: ADR-010 (paved road) — add a contract row; or NEW-ADR on cache identity
proposals.title: Content-addressed cache keys so artefacts are re-obtainable, not just explainable
proposals.detail: Every cache and figure written through the artefact API is stored under a key `blake3(analysis_id || code_version || resolved_params || input_registry_snapshot_hash || lockfile_hash)`, laid out as `cache/<analysis_id>/<key>/{data, meta.json}`. Staleness then becomes an identity check — a key that does not exist means recompute, full stop — rather than a heuristic. This replaces the mtime-vs-last-commit staleness test the audit spec proposes for D4, which cannot see a change in a library module three imports deep. Add one row to the ADR-010 analysis contract: "reads and writes derived data only through the keyed artefact API". Explicitly NOT a workflow engine.
proposals.rationale: S5 proves what produced an artefact; nothing in the design lets you get the artefact back. With 16,779 cache files feeding the figures, and staleness currently judged by mtime, a provenance record saying "this figure came from cache X" is only as good as the guarantee that cache X is current — and the repo already contains the counterexample: `predicted_session_groups.csv` holds a `chron` column that current code cannot produce. Content-addressing makes that class of defect unrepresentable, and it is nearly free here because ADR-004 already computes input hashes and ADR-015 supplies the lockfile hash. It also collapses ADR-014's "the stored null must be current with respect to the analysis code" check into a key comparison instead of a second bespoke staleness mechanism.
proposals.evidence: Audit spec D4: "Per-cache staleness: mtime vs last-commit of the writing script *and* the library modules it imports; validated by a schema/value check (the `predicted_session_groups.csv` `chron` column is the worked example — it holds values current code cannot produce)". Cache scale: 16,779 files / 15.9 GB (audit spec §2, D4). Traceability baseline: 43 of 183 figure-writing scripts use `config.FIGURE_DIR`; non-session figure stems match a source literal 14% of the time.

proposals.target: S5 (success criterion) + §9 Risks row "Gates too strict, exploratory work becomes painful"
proposals.title: Define what an execution log contains, and close the scratch-path provenance hole
proposals.detail: S5 makes the execution log authoritative but never specifies it. Define the run context the artefact API opens: argv, cwd, git sha + dirty flag, lockfile hash, thread-count env allowlist, RNG entropy (ADR-016), host + platform tag + CPU model, resolved BLAS name/version, wall start/end, input registry snapshot id, and tee'd stdout/stderr — written BEFORE the artefact and finalized after, so a crashed run leaves an `incomplete`-marked log rather than none. Separately, scope the notebook/scratch exemption: exempt from GATES, not from PROVENANCE. Artefacts produced on exempt paths are stamped `provenance_tier: scratch` and are mechanically ineligible for an ADR-013 ledger row or a paper figure until re-run through the paved road.
proposals.rationale: "The log is authoritative" is only meaningful if the log's contents are specified; otherwise each component invents its own and S5 becomes another prose rule. The fields above are exactly the ones that determine whether a number can be reproduced, and the crash case matters more than the success case, because a partial artefact with no log is indistinguishable from a good one. The scratch exemption is the more serious issue: as written it is a legal channel for producing untraceable figures, which is precisely the failure the audit is measuring. Exploratory work genuinely needs the exemption; what it does not need is the ability to graduate a scratch figure into the paper without passing through the road.
proposals.evidence: Master design S5 ("execution log (authoritative)" — contents unspecified) and §9 Risks ("notebook/scratch paths are exempt by policy"). Provenance gap measured in audit spec D4 traceability census (43 of 183 figure-writing scripts use `config.FIGURE_DIR`). The required fields follow from the ADR-016 evidence: DYNAMIC_ARCH OpenBLAS 0.3.29 plus variable thread count means host/CPU/BLAS/threads are load-bearing, not decorative — `numpy.show_config()` in the project venv.

proposals.target: ADR-003 (gate list) — two cheap coherence gates
proposals.title: Lockfile-freshness and ledger-lockfile-liveness checks
proposals.detail: Add two mechanical checks to the sub-project 2 gate set. (1) `uv lock --check` fails CI when `uv.lock` has drifted from `pyproject.toml` — this is the gate that would have caught the setup.cfg / environment.yml / .venv divergence measured above, and it is one line of YAML. (2) A ledger-integrity check: every ADR-013 row's `Analysis` commit must resolve in git history, and its recorded lockfile hash must correspond to a lockfile blob reachable from that commit; a row citing an environment no longer present in history fails.
proposals.rationale: Both are near-zero-cost and both target the design's own stated failure mode — a claim whose stated provenance cannot be resolved. Check (1) is the environment-domain instance of ADR-003's shadow-definition principle: the gate exists to stop a second definition of the environment from appearing, which is exactly how the current repo ended up with three. Check (2) makes ADR-013 rows falsifiable; without it, a ledger row is prose that happens to contain a hash.
proposals.evidence: Divergence measured in this repo: setup.cfg (unbounded) vs environment.yml (`numpy<2`) vs installed numpy 2.2.6. Lockfile-check semantics and hash-mandatory design: https://peps.python.org/pep-0751/. ADR-003 currently enumerates gates for constants, imports, session ids, baselines, normalization and provenance — environment is absent from that list.

proposals.target: ADR-007 (approval packet, section "How we know it's right")
proposals.title: Let the packet cite a CI receipt where a gate already covers the component
proposals.detail: Amend the rule to: "How we know it's right" must contain executed output OR a reference to a CI run that produced it (job id + commit sha + the specific check name), never an argument. Keep the hand-pasted executed-output requirement for components whose correctness rests on a bespoke check — the ADR-009 difference report, a new estimator's synthetic recovery, anything touching identity. The no-exemption-for-trivial rule stays untouched.
proposals.rationale: Once the CI tiering and keyed-artefact proposals land, the gates produce exactly the executed output the packet demands, and requiring it to be transcribed by hand into 20-40 packets turns review into a copy-paste exercise. ADR-007 itself names the mechanism that then fails: review degrades into assent when attention is spent on volume rather than substance — the same reason it rejects file-level approval. A CI receipt is STRONGER evidence than pasted output, because it is tied to a commit sha and cannot be edited in transit; the attention saved should go to the sections only a human can check (Provenance, Blast radius, the ADR-009 attribution).
proposals.evidence: Master design ADR-007 rules 1-2 and the (c) alternative's stated failure mode ("review quality collapses from fatigue"). Interacts with the receipt artefact `.ci/receipts/fulldata-<sha>.json` proposed for CI Tier 2, which is designed to be citable in exactly this way.

proposals.target: NEW-ADR (containers) — explicitly defer, and record why
proposals.title: No Apptainer/SIF image at v1; revisit only if HPC job submission enters scope
proposals.detail: Record a deliberate deferral rather than leaving containers unmentioned. The textbook HPC answer is an Apptainer SIF, and it is right for a pipeline whose ANALYSIS runs on the cluster. Here the HPC use is Kilosort4/UnitMatch — already an isolated conda environment producing frozen upstream artefacts that no figure re-derives — while the figure-producing analysis layer is pure-PyPI and portable via `uv.lock`. Adopting containers now adds a build step, a second pin that can drift from the lockfile, and a registry to host. Revisit if master-design Open Question 5 resolves toward HPC job submission in v1, and then containerise only the heavy layer.
proposals.rationale: This is the one place where the field's default advice is heavier than this project needs, and saying so explicitly prevents it being adopted later as unexamined best practice. The reproducibility value of a container over a cross-platform lockfile is system-level dependencies — CUDA, compilers, native libs — and by ADR-002/S8's own design those live outside the layer the paper's reproducibility depends on. Deferring is cheap: the ADR-015 lockfile is a prerequisite for a container image anyway, so nothing is lost by ordering it second.
proposals.evidence: Container-vs-lockfile trade-off for solo researchers and the HPC case for Apptainer: https://apptainer.org/ and https://augmentedscholars.substack.com/p/master-apptainer-in-25-minutes-build. Project split: setup.cfg install_requires is entirely PyPI-with-wheels; environment_unitmatch.yml is the conda-forge/native half (mtscomp, UnitMatchPy, tk). Master design Open Questions, item 5.

overbuilt: A SEED REGISTRY would be a mistake — the brief floats it and it should be rejected. Registering the ~35 distinct seed literals in a canonical module solves nothing: the seed's job is to make one run reproducible, and the run's provenance record is where that belongs. A registry of magic numbers is the shadow-constant pathology (ADR-003's own target) recreated in the RNG domain, with the added harm that two analyses sharing a registered seed get correlated 'independent' null distributions. Register entropy per run, in the log; ban the literal in code.

DVC / DataLad / git-annex are overbuilt at this scale. One user, one box, one branch of data — none of the three's core benefits (branch-switchable data, nested datasets, multi-site distribution) is reachable, while all three add a second add/push discipline and a checkout-mismatch failure mode. The registry's own input hashes, committed as a manifest, cover the measured need. Revisit at dataset-publication time, and then DataLad, not DVC.

BIT-IDENTITY as a reproducibility target should be abandoned before it is attempted. With scipy-openblas built DYNAMIC_ARCH and thread counts differing between the Windows box and an HPC node, bitwise agreement is unattainable for reasons unrelated to the port. Replace with the measured-tolerance floor of ADR-016(c). This SAVES work relative to the current Open Question 4 framing.

Do NOT add a workflow engine (Snakemake / Nextflow / Prefect) to solve the re-execution gap. The unit of work here is one script producing one figure or cache; content-addressed cache keys deliver the reproducibility benefit of a DAG engine without the DSL, the scheduler, and a second place where the session roster gets declared.

ADR-014's 'stored null is current with respect to the analysis code' check should not be built as its own mechanism. It is the cache-staleness problem again. Make the null a keyed artefact and the currency check is a key comparison — one mechanism, not two.

A self-hosted CI runner on the data workstation is the wrong SHAPE of solution, not just a security risk. Even setting aside GitHub's public-repo warning, it makes the box holding the only copy of the data into infrastructure that must stay up and clean. The commit-pinned local receipt gets the same enforcement with none of that coupling.
open_questions: Python 3.12 or 3.13 for the ADR-015 floor? Depends on wheel availability for `pyddm==0.9.0` and `brainglobe-atlasapi` — worth settling with a trial `uv lock` before the ADR is written, since the hard-pinned pyddm is the most likely blocker.

Will the new repo be public or private? It determines whether a self-hosted runner is even on the table, and whether the Tier-1 golden mini-session can be committed (mouse ephys is almost certainly fine, but the licence/ethics position should be stated once rather than assumed).

What is the institutional backup target, and is it the same ceph reached over the X: Samba mount? If so the rclone schedule needs an explicit carve-out from the no-compute-over-Samba hard rule, worded as an I/O exception with an off-hours window.

Can the HPC push outbound (to commit a Tier-3 status file), or must Tier 3 be pull-based — a local job that fetches Slurm results and commits them? This changes the shape of the nightly null-control gate.

How large may the committed golden mini-session be before repo bloat outweighs the CI coverage it unlocks? Set a budget (e.g. <= 20 MB, git-lfs above that) in the sub-project 2 spec rather than discovering it.

Is `data/cache/state_tags/` (29.4 MB) genuinely regenerable after the rebuild, given the state-labeler model itself may be ported with changes? If a port changes its output it is not regenerable in the sense that matters, and it belongs in the backup set with `regenerable=no`.

Must the `numerical-noise` tolerance floor be measured per analysis class BEFORE sub-project 3 starts, or can it be set per component as each lands? Measuring up front costs one bounded experiment; measuring per component risks the floor being chosen after the delta is seen.

reports.overall_verdict: The engineering half of this design is stronger than most systems-neuroscience labs achieve — ADR-009's explained-difference gate is exactly the right posture for a QC rebuild (IBL showed unit yield is dominated by sorter + inclusion criteria, so bit-reproducing old unit counts would be a wrong target), and ADR-011/013/014 exceed field norm. But the design treats QC as a settled layer to be ported, and it is not: unit inclusion, chronic-drift control, track quality and cell-type label confidence are the four places where this specific dataset is most likely to produce a plausible wrong number, and none of them has a first-class home in any ADR. The most serious omission is not a policy gap but an architectural one: QC is currently applied **destructively at ingest** (pkls store spike data only for `good_and_stable` units), so no future "named profile" can ever be more permissive than one unnamed 2025 decision — which makes ADR-011's "decisions are versioned and revisable" false for the single most consequential decision in the pipeline. Second, the cross-stage confound this project has already measured (broad/SPN 89%→15%, median amplitude halving Jun→Jul, at the KS4 detection level) is collinear with the behavioural session gate that excludes 5 of 6 SPN-rich June sessions — so "learning" and "recording epoch" are confounded by construction, and that deserves a contract row, not a memory note. Third, "D1/D2" is not a claim waveform can license at all: with 3 collision-confirmed units (all D1, zero D2), the ledger needs a label-provenance vocabulary or preliminary labels will harden silently. My answer to the lens's framing question is yes on all four counts — named versioned QC profiles, a standing stability control, first-class track-QC fields, and a label-confidence field — but the profiles must be thresholds over a stored metric panel, not a replacement single canonical constant.
matches_best_practice: ADR-009 (explained-difference, not reproduction) is the correct gate for a QC rebuild specifically. IBL's reproducibility study found yield differences across labs largely dissolve once the same sorting pipeline and the same QC filters are applied — i.e. unit counts are a function of inclusion criteria, not of the brain. Demanding reproduction of old unit counts would have enforced the `load_qc_profile() -> {}` defect. https://elifesciences.org/articles/100840

Non-goal §4 'third-party pipelines are wrapped, not reimplemented (KS4, UnitMatch, DANT, Bombcell)' matches where the field has landed — SpikeInterface/Bombcell/UnitRefine are the shared, versioned substrate now, and reimplementing metrics is the main source of silent divergence. https://spikeinterface.readthedocs.io/en/stable/modules/metrics/quality_metrics.html

ADR-011's versioned, attributed, append-only decision log for session inclusion exceeds normal lab practice. The `.bak` evidence (BG_031 losing `19052025` with no recorded reason) is exactly the failure it cures, and it is the right home for unit-level QC decisions once extended.
ADR-013's `retracted`/`refuted` status field plus mandatory effect size + CI exceeds field norm, and is well-matched to an n of thousands of units where p<0.001 is free.
ADR-014's synthetic parameter-recovery requirement for new estimators is above field standard and is the correct answer to 'the null was flat but the estimator measured the wrong thing'.

The project's existing track QC already implements UnitMatch's own recommended validation strategy — independent functional fingerprints (cross-session ISI histogram correlation, held-out ISI AUC 0.7975 on the 312-neuron consensus cohort), two-tracker consensus, and an explicit bimodality detector for the measured matching-failure mode. That is genuinely good practice; it just lives in scripts and module constants instead of the registry. https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11978519/

S5's 'where recorded code and the execution log disagree, the log is authoritative' is a stronger provenance stance than the NWB/DANDI-style metadata most labs manage, and it is the right one for a pipeline whose outputs are unit counts.

proposals.title: Stop applying QC destructively at ingest — spikes for all Kilosort-good units, QC as a view
proposals.detail: Today `core/ingest.py` filters `Cluster` objects to `good_and_stable_ids` before writing the pkl, so units failing the 0.5 Hz / sliding-window-stability / ISI gate have no spike times on disk at all. Every downstream 'unit selection' is therefore a subset of one unnamed 2025 decision, and no named profile can ever be more permissive than it — which silently makes ADR-011's 'decisions are versioned and revisable' false for the most consequential decision in the pipeline. Specify that ingest writes spikes for all KS-good clusters plus a per-unit metric row, and that every QC criterion is applied at analysis time as a named profile over the registry. The storage cost is small: the excluded units are measured at ~0.1 Hz, and `build_session_from_raw(keep_all_good=True)` already exists, so this is a re-ingest from Kilosort output rather than a 228 GB raw re-read.
proposals.rationale: An irreversible filter at ingest is not a QC policy, it is a data-format decision masquerading as one. No registry, ledger or gate downstream can repair it, and it is the reason the June SPN-rich units cannot be re-examined without re-ingest.
proposals.evidence: memory/good_and_stable_ids_definition.md ('pkls store Cluster objects only for good_and_stable units — ingest.py ~line 471'); memory/qc_celltype_yield_investigation_jun2026.md ('pkls store ONLY good_and_stable (can't widen at analysis time → needs re-ingest)'; excluded broad units ~0.1 Hz); e:/python_analysis/git_repos/vis_detect_analysis_Sep2025/src/visdetect/core/qc.py:269-316 (find_good_stable_units, hardcoded 0.5 Hz)

proposals.target: NEW-ADR (QC profiles as first-class versioned registry objects)
proposals.title: Named, hashed, versioned QC profiles — not one canonical firing-rate floor
proposals.detail: The audit's 'four disagreeing firing-rate floors' are not four copies of one number: 0.1 Hz is a sorting-quality floor (`config/qc_profiles.yml`), 0.5 Hz is the Khilkevich stability-port floor (`core/qc.py:316`), 1.0 Hz is an analysis-eligibility floor (`DEFAULT_MIN_FR`, `constants.py:121`). Collapsing them to one canonical constant would destroy real scientific distinctions; the actual defect is that none of them was named. Specify a closed set of ~4 frozen profiles (`sorting_quality`, `striatal_default`, `striatal_strict`, `tracking_eligible`), each a content-hashed dict with an effective date, referenced by id everywhere; a gate bans inline thresholds and bare `min_fr=` kwargs; the ledger and the S5 provenance sidecar record profile id + hash; adding or changing a profile requires an ADR-011 decision-log entry with a reason. Also split each profile into a `quality` block (recording/sorting properties) and an `eligibility` block (enough spikes to estimate the statistic), because `min_median_spikes_per_trial` in today's `default` profile conditions inclusion on task-period firing and belongs in the second.
proposals.rationale: Current field practice is explicit that metric thresholds must be adapted per recording system, region and species — a single global criterion is not achievable, so the enforceable invariant is 'named, versioned and recorded', not 'unique'.
proposals.evidence: https://spikeinterface.readthedocs.io/en/stable/modules/metrics/quality_metrics.html ('the distribution of computed metric values varies depending on recording system, recorded brain areas or species'); e:/.../config/qc_profiles.yml:5-39; e:/.../src/visdetect/core/qc.py:170-229; e:/.../src/visdetect/analysis/constants.py:121

proposals.title: A standing chronic-stability control is a contract row for every across-session claim
proposals.detail: Add a contract row: any analysis comparing sessions separated in time must declare a stability control from a named menu — (a) days-from-implant or session index as a covariate in the model, (b) composition matching or regression on yield / median amplitude / narrow-waveform fraction, (c) tracked-subset replication, (d) within-recording-window comparison — and the ledger gains a `stability_control` field where `none` is legal but visible. This is warranted by measurement, not caution: BG_046's broad/SPN fraction goes 89%→28%→14%→15% at the **KS4 detection level** with median amplitude halving Jun→Jul on an identical channel map, while the behavioural session gate (`min_dprime=0.8`) excludes 5 of 6 SPN-rich June sessions — so learning stage and recording epoch are collinear by construction. Without this row, every Naive→Expert population claim in the new repo inherits a confound that the design currently records only in a memory note.
proposals.rationale: This is the project's largest live threat to scientific validity and the one class of error that ADR-003's mechanical gates and ADR-014's nulls both structurally miss — a label-shuffle null is flat under a real composition drift.
proposals.evidence: memory/qc_celltype_yield_investigation_jun2026.md (89%→15% at detection level; median amplitude 19.8→10.3; identical channel_positions hash across all 46 sessions; 5/6 June sessions manifest-excluded); ADR-013 Verification field currently lists FR-normalisation/circularity/pseudoreplication/per-region/leakage but no stability control

proposals.title: RIGOR-style per-session recording-quality covariates in the registry, computed once at ingest
proposals.detail: Add to the session registry, computed at ingest and versioned with it: days-from-implant, n KS-good units, yield per electrode site, AP-band RMS, median spike amplitude, narrow-waveform fraction, presence-ratio distribution, a drift estimate, and the channel-map hash. This makes the covariates that proposal 3 requires exist as data rather than being re-derived per analysis, and it makes an IBL RIGOR-equivalent session gate available as a named profile (yield ≥0.1 QC-passing units per channel, AP RMS <40 µV, LFP-band derivative <0.05 dB/µm). The channel-map hash in particular is already load-bearing here — it is what ruled out a D-V-sampling explanation for the BG_046 composition drift, and it should be a registry field rather than a one-off investigation.
proposals.rationale: Session-level recording quality is a scientific variable in a chronic learning study, not metadata; storing it once converts a confound into a covariate.
proposals.evidence: https://elifesciences.org/articles/100840 (RIGOR: ≥0.1 units/channel, AP RMS <40 µV, LFP derivative <0.05 dB/µm, median amplitude >50 µV, sliding-refractory <10% contamination at >90% confidence, amplitude cutoff); memory/qc_celltype_yield_investigation_jun2026.md (channel-map hash check)

proposals.target: NEW-ADR (tracked units are defined, versioned objects) — or ADR-004 extension
proposals.title: 'Tracked unit' becomes a registry table with track-level QC fields and a named track-QC profile
proposals.detail: Track quality currently lives as module-level constants in a library file explicitly calibrated to one subject's May-2026 cohort (`tracking_qc.py:26-73`: ISI_PASS 0.75, WAVE_PASS_R 0.95, FR_CV_PASS 0.35, ISI_PEAK_AGREE_PASS 0.85, FUNC_RESP_PASS 0.40 'calibrated to BG_046 cohort distribution'), with hand curation as a code literal (`KNOWN_SUSPECTS: Set[int] = {779, 873, 872}`, line 919). Specify a `tracks` registry table keyed by (subject, track_id, tracker, tracker_version, params_hash) carrying span, per-link match probability, cross-session ISI-histogram correlation, ISI peak-agreement (the detector for the measured matching-failure mode), waveform correlation, depth std, FR CV, held-out ISI AUC, consensus flag, and a verdict from a **named, per-subject-versioned** track-QC profile. Hand verdicts move into the ADR-011 decision log with a reason. Then 'tracked unit' in any claim resolves to (tracker, version, params, profile, verdict) rather than to a filename.
proposals.rationale: The project has measured that 'tracked' is not a reliable predicate here — 56 of 61 long-track UM UIDs were suspect, and the failure mode (tight waveform + bimodal cross-session ISI) is exactly what UnitMatch's own paper says must be checked with independent functional fingerprints.
proposals.evidence: e:/.../src/visdetect/analysis/tracking_qc.py:26-73, 919; memory/tracking_qc_bimodal_isi_finding.md (56 suspect / 4 review / 1 trusted of 61); https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11978519/ (UnitMatch validates with ISI fingerprint, cross-correlation fingerprint and stimulus-response correlation, and warns functional properties must be independently evaluated, not assumed)

proposals.target: NEW-ADR (track-QC calibration) or sub-project 1 spec, tracking section
proposals.title: Per-subject track-QC calibration from within-day splits and (if multi-shank) across-shank controls
proposals.detail: Rather than porting BG_046-calibrated thresholds to BG_031/039/041/049, specify a standing calibration run per subject that reproduces UnitMatch's own controls: split one or more sessions in half, sort each half independently, and match across halves to estimate the within-day false-match and missed-match rates; and, if the probe is multi-shank (the anatomy layer already models `probe_shank_index`), use across-shank pairs as a hard-negative set to estimate the false-positive rate directly. Thresholds are then set from each subject's own calibration curve and stored as a versioned calibration artefact referenced by the track-QC profile id. UnitMatch reports 0.2±0.1% unexpected matches / 4.2±0.8% unexpected non-matches within day and ~1.9% false matches on daily reinsertions, and the across-shank comparison gave outlier rates of 0.037 (UnitMatch) vs 0.009 (DANT) — these are the right reference points for whether this project's consensus cohort is unusually good or unusually bad.
proposals.rationale: It converts track thresholds from a hand-tuned per-cohort judgement into a measured quantity with a stated error rate, which is what a reviewer will ask for when a claim rests on 312 neurons.
proposals.evidence: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11978519/; https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S2666389926000991 (DANT across-shank outlier rate 0.009 vs UnitMatch 0.037, EMD 0.042); e:/.../src/visdetect/anatomy/tracks.py:25-26 (probe_shank_index)

proposals.title: Cell-type label provenance and confidence as required ledger fields, with a hard D1/D2 rule
proposals.detail: Add two required ledger fields: `celltype_label_source` from a controlled vocabulary {optotag_collision_confirmed, optotag_candidate, waveform_gmm, multimodal_classifier, unlabelled} and `celltype_label_confidence` (posterior or held-out AUC, plus the abstain fraction). Add an auditor rule (judgment, not mechanical): a claim whose text names D1 or D2 must either cite units labelled `optotag_collision_confirmed` or state 'putative' with the source named — because waveform features separate narrow from broad, not direct from indirect pathway, and the project has 3 collision-confirmed units, all D1, zero D2. At AUC 0.65 on waveform alone the current labels are below what the field accepts even for the easier narrow/broad contrast (~75% three-way accuracy with optotag ground truth in cortex), and the project's own corpus records that Pvalb/FSI is a continuum rather than a class and that ~6–7% of SPNs co-express D1 and D2.
proposals.rationale: Without a provenance field, a preliminary label propagates through joins into figure legends and hardens into a claim — which is the exact mechanism by which the retracted transient/sustained result became a finding.
proposals.evidence: memory/literature/synthesis-phase3-celltypes.md (Munoz-Manchado: Pvalb gradient not discrete class; Bonnavion 2024: ~6–7% D1/D2 co-expressing SPNs; ≥2 axes required); memory/consensus_cohort_optotagging_figs_jul2026.md (162 putative, 3 collision-confirmed, all D1, 0 D2); memory/talk_substrate_results_jun2026.md (cell-type label AUC 0.65 PRELIMINARY); https://www.nature.com/articles/s41467-019-10716-w (~75% three-way discriminability with optotag ground truth; FSI classification from rate+waveform 'may not be reliable')

proposals.target: Sub-project 1 Foundation spec (QC layer) — companion to the profiles ADR
proposals.title: Compute a standard quality-metric panel once at ingest; profiles become thresholds over stored metrics
proposals.detail: Specify that ingest emits a per-unit metric table using the field's standard definitions rather than bespoke ones — sliding-refractory-period contamination confidence, amplitude cutoff, presence ratio, SNR, median amplitude, and a drift metric — taken from SpikeInterface/Bombcell, with the Khilkevich sliding-window stability statistic retained as a named metric for continuity with the reference lineage rather than as the only gate. Profiles then threshold stored columns, so changing a profile is a re-filter (seconds) rather than a re-computation, and the ledger's profile hash fully determines the unit set. Amplitude cutoff and presence ratio matter specifically here: they are the metrics that quantify BG_046's Jun→Jul amplitude halving and would turn 'real chronic drift' from a narrative into a per-session number.
proposals.rationale: Storing metrics separately from decisions is what makes ADR-011-style versioned, revisable QC decisions physically possible, and using standard definitions removes a whole class of same-name-different-behaviour divergence at the tool boundary.
proposals.evidence: https://github.com/Julie-Fabre/bombcell (17 metrics, good/MUA/noise/non-somatic, MATLAB and Python); https://spikeinterface.readthedocs.io/en/stable/modules/metrics/quality_metrics.html (contamination vs completeness metric families); e:/.../src/visdetect/core/qc.py:170-206 (current panel: n_spikes, mean_rate, isi_violations_frac, median_spikes_per_trial only)

proposals.target: Sub-project 1 Foundation spec (QC layer) — filter semantics
proposals.title: Fail closed on unknown metrics; make 'unknown' a tri-state, not a silent pass
proposals.detail: `apply_unit_filters` currently does `out['isi_violations_frac'].fillna(0.0) <= max_isi_viol_frac` (a unit with an unmeasurable ISI metric passes the contamination gate) and, when `is_good_cluster` is absent, silently sets `require_good_cluster = False` — i.e. a missing input becomes a permissive decision. This is the same failure class as `load_qc_profile` returning `{}`, and it is invisible for the same reason. Specify that every metric is tri-state pass/fail/unknown, that `unknown` fails by default, that a profile may opt into `unknown_is_pass` per metric explicitly, and that the per-session QC report prints counts per state so an unexpected `unknown` population is visible rather than absorbed.
proposals.rationale: The rebuild's stated motivation is that a plausible wrong number is worse than a crash; fail-open defaults are the mechanism that produces plausible wrong unit counts.
proposals.evidence: e:/.../src/visdetect/core/qc.py:186-196 (fillna(0.0) pass; require_good_cluster silently disabled at line 190); memory/new_repo_rebuild_aug2026.md defect #2 (load_qc_profile miss swallowed by `return {}`)

proposals.title: Profile-sensitivity is a precondition for promoting a claim from exploratory to confirmed
proposals.detail: Require that any claim moving from `exploratory` to `confirmed` be re-run under a second named QC profile — and, where applicable, with and without the tracked-subset restriction — with the effect size under each recorded in the ledger row. This is cheap once profiles are thresholds over a stored metric panel (proposal 8), it is mechanically checkable (the row either has two effect sizes or it does not), and it targets precisely the failure this project has already suffered twice. Name which comparator applies per claim class: a stricter profile tests contamination-driven effects, a looser one tests yield/selection-driven effects, and they are not interchangeable.
proposals.rationale: Single-cluster quality metrics are known to be weak inclusion criteria — clusters with identical ISI-violation fractions span ~5% to ~50% false-discovery rate — while population-level estimates are robust, so the honest instrument is sensitivity across thresholds rather than a defensible single threshold.
proposals.evidence: https://www.eneuro.org/content/11/8/ENEURO.0554-23.2024 (ISIv inappropriate as a single-cluster inclusion criterion; population-level FDR estimates robust); ADR-013 currently has a Status field but no promotion criterion

proposals.target: §6 known-defect register / sub-project 0 audit spec D8 seed table
proposals.title: Five ephys-specific register entries with directions of effect
proposals.detail: Add, each with a stated direction so ADR-009 can attribute deltas: (i) irreversible ingest-time QC — every published unit count is a subset of one unnamed profile, so counts under any new profile can only fall, never rise, without re-ingest; (ii) BG_046 detection-composition drift — early sessions are SPN/high-amplitude biased and late sessions FSI/low-amplitude biased, so any Naive→Expert cell-type contrast is inflated in the direction of the drift; (iii) BG_046-calibrated track-QC thresholds applied to other subjects — direction unknown, **quarantine**; (iv) BG_031 Laser-event extraction gap, 35 of 43 sessions missing — optotag yield for BG_031 is understated and no negative claim about D2 yield is supportable; (v) `KNOWN_SUSPECTS = {779, 873, 872}` hardcoded — the tracked cohort is slightly cleaner than an uncurated one by an unmeasured amount. Entry (iv) matters because it is a data-completeness defect that looks like a biological result.
proposals.rationale: The register's stated job is to let a delta be tagged `known-defect` rather than `unexplained`; without ephys entries, every QC-layer delta in sub-project 3 is unexplained by definition and blocks.
proposals.evidence: memory/consensus_cohort_optotagging_figs_jul2026.md (8/43 BG_031 pkls carry a Laser event; user states optotagging was designed for every session → NI-DAQ extraction gap, not real coverage); memory/qc_celltype_yield_investigation_jun2026.md; e:/.../src/visdetect/analysis/tracking_qc.py:52-57, 919

proposals.title: Add sorter and tracker provenance as a required provenance element
proposals.detail: The five parts (execution log, code, environment, inputs = registry snapshot + decision-log revision, git sha) do not capture what produced the spikes: Kilosort4 version and parameter hash, drift-correction settings, UnitMatch version and parameters, DANT version, and the metric-panel version. These sit upstream of the registry snapshot, they change unit counts and match sets, and they are exactly the kind of thing that is remembered rather than recorded. Store them per session in the registry so 'inputs' resolves to them transitively, and state explicitly in S5 that they are part of the input element.
proposals.rationale: A figure whose provenance records the analysis commit but not the sorter version is not reproducible in the sense that matters for a QC-sensitive claim, and this project already has one live case of a sorter/extraction change (the March-2026 MATLAB lick re-extraction) invalidating downstream registries.
proposals.evidence: master design §3 S5; memory/lick_channel_defect_jul2026.md (re-extraction under-detects licks 10–40× in 33 sessions); memory/new_repo_rebuild_aug2026.md defect #12 (stale tf_responsive registries loaded with no gate after the lick-channel fix)

proposals.target: S1 (one definition per constant) + ADR-003 gates
proposals.title: Let the constants registry hold registered named variants, so intentional divergence is declared rather than hidden
proposals.detail: S1's gate as written would fail live code that is deliberately and correctly divergent: `tracking_qc.py:79-80` defines `BIG_POOL = {2.0, 4.0}` / `SMALL_POOL = {1.25, 1.35}` with a comment saying it intentionally differs from `constants.{BIG,SMALL}_CHANGE_SIZES` because the tracking-QC spec treats 1.5× as ambiguous. Add a registered-variant mechanism — e.g. `CHANGE_SIZE_POOLS['tracking_qc_v1']` — so the canonical module owns every value and the variant carries a name, an owner and a one-line reason. Without this, the first legitimate divergence teaches everyone to hide values inside dicts or YAML where the AST gate cannot see them, and S1 decays exactly as the prose rule did.
proposals.rationale: Gates that cannot express a correct exception get routed around; the enforceable invariant is 'registered', not 'unique'.

proposals.title: Scope the null-control gate to analyses that produce a ledger claim
proposals.detail: 'Every analysis ships a null control and its recorded output must be flat' is undefined for the QC layer's descriptive outputs — a per-session unit-count census, a yield-vs-time table, or a metric-distribution report has no meaningful label shuffle, and forcing one produces ceremonial nulls that dilute the rule where it matters. Scope clause 1 to analyses that write a row in the ADR-013 ledger, and require descriptive/QC-census scripts to declare `null: not_applicable` with a one-line reason instead. Clause 2 (synthetic recovery for new estimators) should keep its full scope — it applies squarely to QC and tracking estimators such as the held-out ISI AUC and the track-verdict scoring.
proposals.rationale: A gate that fires on outputs it cannot judge trains people to satisfy it mechanically, which is how `check_refactor_guardrails.py` reached 84% phantom violations and stopped being read.
proposals.evidence: master design ADR-014 clause 1; sub-project 0 audit spec D5 (218 real vs 1,375 reported violations)

overbuilt: ADR-014's 'every analysis ships a null control' applied to QC censuses and metric inventories — there is no surrogate for 'how many units passed profile X in session Y'. Scope it to ledger-claim-producing analyses; keep the synthetic-recovery clause at full scope.

ADR-010's AST structural-similarity duplicate gate will fire constantly on QC code that is legitimately near-identical by design — `badge_isi`, `badge_wave`, `badge_depth`, `badge_fr_cv` are all thin wrappers over `_badge_threshold` (tracking_qc.py:508-548). Exempt registered metric/badge families or the gate becomes noise the way the existing guardrail script did.

Building a Bombcell/SpikeInterface *wrapper API* is the wrong shape. Run the tool and store its own output table keyed by (session, cluster_id) with the tool version; a wrapper creates a second name for every metric, which is the exact divergence class the rebuild exists to kill.

ADR-007 packets for the QC layer should not each carry a hand-written 'how we know it's right'. Standardise one auto-generated QC evidence block — units in/out per session per profile, before/after counts, and the metric distributions — so the 20-40 packets stay reviewable rather than stalling on bespoke prose.

Do not extend ADR-012's confirmatory-cohort mechanism to unit level (e.g. a held-out tracked cohort). With 312 consensus neurons and 1 strict Naive→Expert track, there is no power for it, and the session-level field plus deferral is the right call as already decided.
open_questions: Can re-ingest with `keep_all_good=True` recover spike times for all KS-good units from Kilosort output alone, without re-reading the ~228 GB `.ap.bin`? Memory says yes for spikes but that RawWaveforms exist only for good_and_stable units — which determines whether the waveform-dependent half of the metric panel (SNR, non-somatic, amplitude) needs raw access. Sub-project 0 should measure this on one session; it decides whether proposal 1 is cheap or a project.

Are implant dates recorded for all six striatal subjects? Days-from-implant is the cheapest stability covariate in proposal 3 and is unusable if the date is not in the experiment metadata; session index within subject is a weaker but always-available fallback.

Is the chronic probe here multi-shank? The anatomy layer models `probe_shank_index`, which would make UnitMatch's across-shank false-positive control directly available at near-zero cost. If single-shank, the within-day split-half control is the only option and requires one re-sort per subject.

Which second QC profile is the sensitivity comparator for a given claim class — stricter (tests contamination-driven effects) or looser (tests yield/selection-driven effects)? These test different failure modes and the design should name one per claim class rather than leaving it to the analyst.

Should sessions failing the behavioural gate (`min_trials=150`, `min_dprime=0.8`) still be ingested and QC'd, so recording-composition trends can be measured over the full 46-session BG_046 series independently of behavioural inclusion? Currently 18 of 46 sessions never enter the pipeline and they are disproportionately the SPN-rich early ones, which is precisely what makes the drift confound unmeasurable from inside the analysed set.

Does the new repo want a subject-agnostic normalised track-quality score (percentile within cohort, or held-out ISI AUC) as the versioned object, instead of per-subject threshold sets? A normalised score is more portable across the six subjects but makes 'trusted' relative rather than absolute, which has its own reporting cost.

reports.lens: Lens 5 — Publication readiness and collaboration future-proofing (senior-PI view)
reports.overall_verdict: On the axes this design was written for — provenance, definition uniqueness, exclusion attribution, multiplicity honesty — it is well above what I see in most Nature-tier systems-neuroscience labs. ADR-011's append-only decision log with attributed reasons is a better answer to the Nature Reporting Summary's "data exclusions" field and ARRIVE Item 3 than almost any lab produces, and ADR-013's ledger with a `retracted`/`refuted` status field plus mandatory effect size + CI is genuinely ahead of the field. ADR-010's pre-specification requirement (prediction + falsifier + SESOI, committed before the run) is free timestamped preregistration that will materially strengthen the paper. But the design is built entirely for *internal* correctness and has no manuscript-facing layer: the words "manuscript", "figure panel", "sex", "genotype", "NWB", "DANDI", "DOI", "CITATION", "lockfile", "source data" and "onboarding" appear nowhere in the master design. The three retrofit-expensive omissions are (1) realized n at every level per artefact, (2) subject/acquisition metadata in the registry, and (3) an environment *lock* rather than an environment *description* — all three are cheap to add to ADR-004/S5 now and require re-running the whole pipeline to add later. The human-onboarding gap is real but cheap; sub-project 5 specifies an AI layer and no human one.
matches_best_practice: ADR-011 (versioned, append-only, attributed decision log; manifests as build artefacts) directly satisfies ARRIVE 2.0 Item 3 — 'report any animals, experimental units or data points not included in the analysis and explain why' — and the Nature Reporting Summary's Data Exclusions field, which requires a positive disclosure even when nothing was excluded. Most labs cannot answer this at review time; this design answers it by construction.

ADR-013's mandatory effect size + CI in the same row as the claim is exactly right at this project's n. With thousands of units, p < 0.001 is available for biologically meaningless effects — the Reporting Summary's statistics section asks for effect sizes and CIs precisely for this reason.

ADR-013's `status` field (exploratory/confirmed/retracted/refuted) plus 'superseded by' is stronger than the field norm. A project that shows its retractions reads as more trustworthy to a reviewer, not less, and this repo already has two (transient/sustained; sustained-StimSens).

ADR-010's pseudoreplication declaration — a required clustering variable plus mixed-effects/cluster-robust method wherever n_units >> n_sessions >> n_subjects — pre-answers the single most common Nature-tier reviewer objection to rodent ephys, and pre-answers the Reporting Summary's 'whether measurements were taken from distinct samples or the same sample measured repeatedly'.

ADR-010's pre-specification requirement is timestamped preregistration at zero extra cost, and ADR-012 states the residual forking-paths risk plainly rather than hiding it. That paragraph is close to publishable as a limitations statement.

S8 (`pip install -e .[analysis]` in a clean env with no UnitMatch/GPU/MATLAB dependency) is exactly what a reviewer or a rotation student needs. Nature journals encourage supplying source code, install guide and sample data for reviewer checking; S8 makes that a one-liner instead of a project. https://www.nature.com/nature-portfolio/editorial-policies/reporting-standards

ADR-014's synthetic parameter recovery before real-data application is above field standard for a single lab and is the correct answer to 'does your estimator measure what you think it measures' — a question reviewers ask about novel estimators (the kernel-width and latent-decomposition estimators here will attract it).

MIT LICENSE is already present and is the right choice for research code — permissive, no downstream friction for reviewers or collaborators. (e:/python_analysis/git_repos/vis_detect_analysis_Sep2025/LICENSE)

proposals.title: Provenance sidecar must carry a realized n-table, not just the inputs that could reconstruct one
proposals.detail: S5 records inputs as 'registry snapshot + decision-log revision'. That reconstructs the roster in principle but does not record the *realized* n after every filter at the moment the artefact was written. Add a mandatory `n_table` block to the sidecar: n_subjects, n_sessions, n_units, n_trials, per-condition trial counts, per-panel n if the figure has panels, and the declared clustering variable (which ADR-010 already forces the analysis to name). Make it a gate: an artefact whose sidecar has no n_table fails, the same way an artefact with no provenance fails today. This is the highest-value single addition in this review because every journal asks for exact n per group per panel, and the only way to add it later is to re-run everything.
proposals.rationale: The Nature Reporting Summary requires 'the exact sample size (n) for each experimental group/condition, given as a discrete number and unit of measurement' and a statement on distinct-vs-repeated measurement; ARRIVE Item 2 requires exact numbers per group and the total. At submission you will be assembling these by hand across ~40 panels, and any hand-assembled n disagrees with the figure sooner or later — ADR-011 already documents that two figures in this repo can silently disagree on n.
proposals.evidence: https://www.nature.com/nature-portfolio/editorial-policies/reporting-standards ; https://arriveguidelines.org/sites/arrive/files/documents/Author%20Checklist%20-%20E10%20only.pdf ; master design lines 61 and 349 (e:/python_analysis/git_repos/vis_detect_analysis_Sep2025/docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-05-new-repo-master-design.md)

proposals.title: Registry gains a subjects table and a per-session acquisition table (ARRIVE + DANDI aligned)
proposals.detail: ADR-004's registry schema is 'subject, session, date, variant, artefact paths, provenance'. Add a `subjects` table — species (Mus musculus), strain/line, genotype (ChR2-Cre + AAV construct), sex, DOB, ethics/project-licence number, surgery date, implant coordinates and hemisphere — and a per-session acquisition table — age-at-session (derived), weight/water-restriction status, probe serial, IMRO/channel-map, insertion depth, rig, sorter name+version+params, TPrime parameters, training stage. None of these are in the design; the word 'sex' does not appear in it. All are trivially recordable now from lab notes and effectively unrecoverable in two years, and every one is required either by ARRIVE Item 8, the Reporting Summary's research-animals section, or DANDI's subject metadata.
proposals.rationale: Single-sex cohorts are a live reviewer flashpoint in 2026 and the Reporting Summary forces a positive disclosure with justification; 'hemisphere = LEFT' is already a memory-note-level fact rather than a data-level fact in this project, which is exactly how such facts get lost. DANDI additionally *requires* subject_id and species on every NWB file and strongly expects sex/age/genotype.
proposals.evidence: https://docs.dandiarchive.org/user-guide-sharing/dandiset-metadata/ ; https://journals.plos.org/plosbiology/article?id=10.1371%2Fjournal.pbio.3000411 ; ADR-004, master design lines 156-173

proposals.title: Require an environment lock and an external-tool version table, not a version list
proposals.detail: S5 says the environment is recorded as 'language + every package version'. A recorded version list describes an environment; it does not recreate one. Require instead that the sidecar carry a hash pointing at a committed lockfile (uv.lock / conda-lock / pip-compile output) plus an `external_tools` table for everything outside pip that ADR-002 explicitly wraps: Kilosort 4 commit, UnitMatch version, DANT version, Bombcell version, MATLAB release, CUDA/driver, SpikeGLX/TPrime version. Without the second table the sidecar silently omits the tools that actually determine spike times and unit identity.
proposals.rationale: The reviewer-facing promise of S5 is 'this figure can be regenerated'. A pip freeze from 2026 will not resolve in 2028, and the heavy stack (KS4/UnitMatch/MATLAB) is where the numerical differences that matter live — it is the layer ADR-009's explained-difference gate is least able to attribute if it moves silently.
proposals.evidence: master design line 61 (S5) and ADR-002 lines 106-121; https://elifesciences.org/reviewed-preprints/110170 (spike-sorting pipeline reproducibility)

proposals.title: A paper layer: manuscript panel IDs, a figure manifest, and one-command regeneration
proposals.detail: Add a top layer above figures in which each manuscript panel has a stable id (`F3b`, `ED2a`, `S7c`) and a manifest row binding it to: the producing component + commit, the registry snapshot, the decision-log revision, the environment lock, the sidecar n_table, and the ledger row(s) whose claims it supports. Ship `visdetect repro F3b` that resolves the manifest, verifies the environment and registry snapshot, and regenerates or verifies-from-cache. Add a CI smoke job that runs the repro path for two panels on one session so it cannot rot. This also kills the `fig3_v2_final_FINAL.png` problem during revision by giving figures typed identity, exactly as ADR-004 gave sessions typed identity.
proposals.rationale: Nature journals mandate a code availability statement and several Nature titles peer-review custom code central to the findings; the practical question a reviewer or editor asks is 'can I get Figure 3 back'. S5 gives per-artefact provenance but nothing binds an artefact to a *manuscript panel*, and during revision you will regenerate every panel several times. Retrofitting panel identity after the figures exist is the same class of work as retrofitting session identity, which is why this rebuild is happening.
proposals.evidence: https://www.nature.com/nature-portfolio/editorial-policies/reporting-standards ; https://www.nature.com/articles/s41562-021-01190-w (Nature Human Behaviour code review) ; master design §7 lines 568-577 (no paper layer in the decomposition)

proposals.title: Sub-project 5 must produce a human layer as well as an AI layer
proposals.detail: §7 lists sub-project 5 as 'Generated CLAUDE.md, skills, hooks, curated memory'. There is no human-facing deliverable anywhere in the decomposition. Extend it to emit README.md and docs/ from the same generator that emits CLAUDE.md (module map, gate list, constants table, install instructions — generate-don't-restate applies identically), and add three hand-written pages that a generator cannot produce: (a) a 30-minute walkthrough that installs the analysis extra and runs one analysis end-to-end on one session to a figure; (b) a task/vocabulary glossary (go vs catch by change_size, the `fa` ≠ SDT-FA trap, EVENT_VALID_OUTCOMES, the state labels and their circularity caveat); (c) a data-provenance page: where raw lives, how raw becomes a session, what the registry is. Additionally, keep the ADR-007 approval packets as a browsable, indexed corpus rather than discarding them after approval — 20–40 plain-language 'what it is / why it exists / how we know it's right' documents *are* the onboarding manual and the Methods first draft.
proposals.rationale: A rotation student in a year, a collaborator on the multi-subject paper, and a reviewer handed the repo all need the same thing, and none of them read CLAUDE.md. The `fa` ≠ SDT-false-alarm distinction alone is a result-destroying trap that currently lives only in AI-facing prose; a human who gets it wrong produces a plausible wrong number, which is the failure mode ADR-007 exists to catch.

proposals.title: Make the session model provably NWB-convertible now, with a one-session NeuroConv test
proposals.detail: Add an export contract to the foundation spec: the session model must be losslessly convertible to NWB, demonstrated once by converting a single real session with NeuroConv and passing nwbinspector at DANDI's configuration. Concretely this constrains four things now — (1) the registry's SubjectID/SessionKey must have a declared mapping to `sub-<id>_ses-<id>`; (2) the trials table must carry `start_time`/`stop_time` alongside the task columns; (3) the units table must carry spike_times, quality metrics, waveform_mean and an electrode reference; (4) SpikeGLX .meta, IMRO and sorter version must be preserved rather than consumed. You are not depositing now; you are ensuring deposit is a week rather than a quarter.
proposals.rationale: The eventual deposit target for chronic Neuropixels is DANDI, which requires NWB with subject_id and species and organises assets by subject and session id. The pkl is a bespoke dataclass, and the design contains no statement about external format at all. The expensive part of a late deposit is never the conversion code — it is discovering that the acquisition metadata NeuroConv reads was thrown away three years earlier.
proposals.evidence: https://docs.dandiarchive.org/user-guide-sharing/validating-files/ ; https://nwb-overview.readthedocs.io/en/latest/conversion_tutorial/06_dandi.html ; https://neuroconv.readthedocs.io/en/main/ ; https://proceedings.scipy.org/articles/cehj4257

proposals.title: Every figure emits a tidy source_data.csv of exactly the plotted values
proposals.detail: Have the artefact API write, next to each figure and its provenance sidecar, a tidy CSV of the values actually plotted (one row per point/bar/line-sample, with the grouping columns and the n per group). This is near-free at write time because the plotting call already has the arrays. It buys three things at once: it satisfies journal source-data requests without a scramble, it makes the ADR-013 ledger's effect sizes independently auditable, and it lets the repro path verify a figure by diffing numbers rather than pixels — which matters because matplotlib versions change rendering but not data.
proposals.rationale: Source data files are routinely requested at Nature-tier revision, and assembling them retrospectively from 36 GB of PNGs is impossible. It also solves the figure-comparison problem ADR-009 creates: comparing old vs new *numbers* is tractable; comparing old vs new images is not.
proposals.evidence: https://www.nature.com/nature-portfolio/editorial-policies/reporting-standards ; audit spec D4 traceability census, lines 129-136 (e:/python_analysis/git_repos/vis_detect_analysis_Sep2025/docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-06-subproject-0-audit-spec.md)

proposals.title: CITATION.cff, a data license, paper-freeze tags and a Zenodo DOI
proposals.detail: Four small, one-time items with no ongoing cost. (1) Add CITATION.cff with the author's ORCID so the repo is citable and so Zenodo's GitHub integration populates release metadata correctly — note that if a .zenodo.json is also present it wins and the CITATION.cff is ignored, so pick one. (2) Declare a *data* license explicitly: MIT covers code only, and DANDI deposits need an open data licence (CC0 or CC-BY-4.0) — decide now because it affects what consent/ethics language you need. (3) Define a `paper-freeze/<name>` tag convention: at submission and at each revision, tag the repo and mint a Zenodo DOI for that exact state. (4) Write the data-availability and code-availability statements as living files in the repo, generated where possible from the registry.
proposals.rationale: Nature journals mandate a code availability statement naming the location and accessibility of custom code, and Nature Methods and peers expect a persistent identifier (DOI) rather than a bare GitHub URL, because a branch can move and a DOI cannot. The current repo has MIT for code and nothing for data.
