proposals.target: NEW-ADR (ADR-017) or extend ADR-013 — generated reporting pack
proposals.title: Generate the ARRIVE E10 and Reporting Summary drafts from registry + decision log + ledger
proposals.detail: Add `docs/reporting/` holding two generated documents: an ARRIVE 2.0 Essential-10 checklist and a Nature Reporting Summary draft. Most fields are already derivable — Item 2 sample size from the n_table, Item 3 inclusion/exclusion from the decision log, Item 8 animals from the new subjects table, the statistics section from the ledger's effect-size/CI/test columns, software/code from the environment lock. The residual hand-written fields are few and should be stated as explicit negative disclosures: no a-priori power calculation (observational chronic-recording design, state why), no randomisation (single-cohort longitudinal, N/A), and blinding — where you should positively record that the blinded session sorter was used, since that is a genuine methodological strength currently buried in scripts/session_sorting/.
proposals.rationale: Both forms demand a positive disclosure even when the answer is 'not applicable' — a blank field is a query from the editorial office. Generating them keeps the same generate-don't-restate guarantee ADR-005 gives CLAUDE.md, so the checklist cannot drift from the analysis the way the current CLAUDE.md constants table drifted from constants.py.
proposals.evidence: https://arriveguidelines.org/sites/arrive/files/documents/ARRIVE%20guidelines%202.0%20-%20English.pdf ; https://www.nature.com/documents/nr-reporting-summary-flat.pdf ; ADR-005 lines 175-194

proposals.title: Add preregistration, experimental-unit and figure-panel columns to the ledger row
proposals.detail: Three columns, each cheap and each answering a question a reviewer will ask. (1) `prespec_commit` — the sha and date of the ADR-010 pre-specification that predicted this claim, making the preregistration machine-readable rather than an assertion. (2) `experimental_unit` — mouse / session / unit, stated explicitly per claim; this is ARRIVE Item 1 and it is the field that stops a units-as-n claim from reaching a figure caption. (3) `figure_panels` — which manuscript panels the claim appears in, closing the loop with the ADR-015 manifest so that a retracted ledger row immediately names the figures it invalidates.
proposals.rationale: ADR-012 says plainly that readers should know which protections applied to which result and that the ledger is where they will find out — but the ledger as specified has no preregistration field, so it cannot actually answer that. The experimental-unit column also converts ADR-010's pseudoreplication declaration from an engineering artefact into a reportable scientific fact.
proposals.evidence: master design ADR-013 table lines 470-481; ADR-012 lines 459-466; ADR-010 line 348 (pre-specification); https://arriveguidelines.org/sites/arrive/files/documents/Author%20Checklist%20-%20E10%20only.pdf

proposals.title: State explicitly that no figure produced by the old repo may enter the manuscript
proposals.detail: ADR-009 deliberately makes the old repo not a reproduction target, and the audit measures that the old FIGURES tree is largely untraceable to a producing script. Those two facts together mean any old figure carried into the paper is unprovenanced by design. Add a one-line rule to sub-project 6: every manuscript panel is regenerated in the new repo under ADR-015's manifest; old figures are archived as history and are ineligible for the manuscript. Also archive the frozen old repo tag to Zenodo so that anything cited from it has a resolvable identifier.
proposals.rationale: Without this rule the 36 GB of untraceable figures becomes a slow leak into the paper — a panel gets reused 'because it's already made' and then cannot be regenerated when a reviewer asks. Stating it now also correctly sizes sub-project 4: the figure layer must be able to make every paper panel, which is a scoping fact the specs need.
proposals.evidence: audit spec D4 traceability census lines 129-136 and §6 non-goals lines 242-243; master design §9 risk table lines 615-623

proposals.title: Declare an explicit descriptive-artefact exemption class rather than allowing token nulls
proposals.detail: For genuinely descriptive artefacts — an exemplar raster, an ISI histogram, a learning curve, a unit-yield table — a null control is meaningless, and a gate that demands one will be satisfied by a null nobody believes. Add a declared `descriptive` class: the analysis states in its docstring that it makes no inferential claim, the ledger records it as descriptive with no effect-size row required, and the gate accepts the declaration instead of a null. This tightens rather than weakens the gate, because the exemption is recorded and auditable and a descriptive artefact then cannot be cited as evidence for a claim.
proposals.rationale: Gates that can be satisfied by ritual teach people to perform the ritual, which is precisely how the current repo's prose rules failed. Making the exemption explicit also produces a useful publication fact: which panels are illustrative and which are inferential — a distinction reviewers police and authors routinely blur.
proposals.evidence: ADR-014 lines 504-534; the project's own rule that fixes are proven by execution not argument (ADR-007 rule 2, lines 238-240)

proposals.title: Machine-generate four of the six packet sections so the human writes only two
proposals.detail: Provenance, blast radius, 'how we know it's right' (the executed check output) and the ADR-009 attributed delta are all mechanically derivable from the repo — imports give blast radius, git gives provenance, the test run gives output, the difference report gives the delta. Have the tooling emit a pre-filled packet, leaving the human to write 'what it is' and 'why it exists' in plain language and to record the decision. This preserves the gate's actual function — a scientist reading a legible explanation — while removing the transcription work that is most likely to make a 20–40-packet process stall at packet 9.
proposals.rationale: Not a relitigation of ADR-007; the packet count and the no-trivial-exemption rule stand. This is about survival: the packets are also your Methods corpus and your onboarding manual, so the process must be cheap enough to finish. It is the same argument ADR-005 makes about CLAUDE.md — the derivable parts should be derived.
proposals.evidence: ADR-007 lines 216-253; ADR-009 line 321 (the packet must now also carry the attributed delta, increasing per-packet cost)

overbuilt: ADR-009's explained-difference gate applied uniformly to every ported component. From a publication standpoint only the components feeding manuscript panels need full per-component delta attribution; a plotting utility or an exploratory screening script does not. Suggest tiering by ADR-015's manifest — components tagged `paper-critical` get the full attributed-delta report, everything else gets a one-line changed/unchanged note — so the port's effort concentrates where a reviewer will look. This is sequencing, not weakening: the gate stays, its depth is prioritised.

ADR-014's synthetic parameter recovery for *every new estimator*. For estimators that are thin wrappers over well-characterised primitives (a bootstrap CI, an AUROC, an FDR correction) recovery on synthetic data proves only that scipy works. Scope the requirement to estimators with free parameters or latent structure — the hazard-accumulator latents, kernel width, coding directions, decoders — which is where it actually earns its keep and where it would have caught the circularity bug.

The two-stage spec process (§8) writing all six specs in one dedicated session. Specs 4 (figures/artefacts) and 5 (AI layer) depend on decisions that only become concrete once the foundation exists, and the additions proposed here (manuscript layer, n-table, NWB export contract) will shift spec 4 substantially. Consider writing specs 1-3 together for mutual consistency and deferring 4-6 to a second sitting after the foundation lands — the cross-spec consistency pass still runs over all six.

ADR-013's `Verification` free-text column listing which battery was applied. This will drift into inconsistent prose. Make it an enumerated set of booleans (fr_normalised, circularity_checked, pseudoreplication_handled, per_region_breakdown, leakage_controlled, trial_count_matched) so it is queryable and so 'which of my claims lack a leakage control' is a one-line answer rather than a reading exercise.
open_questions: What is actually being deposited, and where? Raw SpikeGLX .bin for ~6 chronically-implanted subjects is many TB; processed NWB (spike times, trials, units, quality metrics, waveforms) is order tens of GB and is what DANDI is built for. This decision determines what the registry must carry and should be made before the foundation spec is written, not at submission.

Is the cohort single-sex? The Reporting Summary forces a positive disclosure with justification and this is a common reviewer query in 2026. If sex is mixed, it needs to be a registry field and a covariate consideration; if single-sex, the justification needs writing now while the reason is still known.

Who is the second author/analyst likely to be, and does the multi-subject paper involve data from another lab member's animals? If yes, the registry needs a data-origin/consent field and the decision log needs a `who` that is not always the same person — ADR-011 specifies 'who decided' but the design assumes one decider throughout.
Does the ethics/project licence permit open data deposit of these recordings, and is there a licence number to record? This is a five-minute question now and a submission blocker later.

What happens to the ~11 published/presented results in docs/science that came from the old repo? Under ADR-009 they are not reproduction targets, but ADR-013's ledger has to be seeded with them at some status — are they imported as `exploratory` pending regeneration in the new repo, or are they only admitted once regenerated?

Is the blinded session sorter (scripts/session_sorting/, 133 manual sorts) intended to appear in the paper as a blinding procedure? If so it needs to survive migration as a first-class analysis with its own ledger row and its hand-labels tracked in git — currently they are gitignored and exist on one disk.

reports.lens: Lens 6 — Adversarial critic: overbuild, failure modes, and what will actually happen
reports.overall_verdict: The diagnosis is excellent and several ADRs (004 typed identity, 009 explained-difference, 011 versioned decision log, S5 provenance) are better than what most systems-neuroscience labs run. The design's failure is not in any single ADR but in their sum: it prices each gate against the defect it prevents, and never prices the total against the researcher's available hours. Measured on the live repo, the packet estimate in ADR-007 is off by 2-3x (64 non-init library modules, 40 of them in `src/visdetect/analysis/` at 19,268 LOC, plus ~15-20 implied gates → 70-100 packets, not 20-40), and the ADR-010 contract + ADR-013 ledger + ADR-014 nulls add roughly 8-25 h of ceremony to an exploratory analysis that today takes 3-6 h to write. That is a 3-5x tax with no exploratory tier, and the stated escape ("notebook/scratch paths exempt by policy") is the exact loophole through which all 378 old scripts would pass — every one of them was scratch until it produced a figure. There is no time budget, no stop-loss, no port sunset criterion, and no policy for the 63 unmerged commits of live science on 5 branches (one committed today). A pragmatic top-tier lab would keep ADR-004/009/011 and S5, gate on *promotion to a claim* rather than on file creation, demote the AST duplicate checker to a periodic audit, and time-box the whole rebuild with an explicit fallback.
matches_best_practice: ADR-009's explained-difference gate is the single best decision in the document. Making `unexplained` the only failing verdict — rather than bit-reproduction — is rarer and more correct than what most labs do when rebuilding, and it correctly refuses to spend the port proving it can regenerate known defects.

ADR-011 (append-only decision log; staging manifests as generated build artefacts, never hand-edited) is the highest value-per-hour item in the whole design. It directly closes the `.bak` incident where BG_031 lost session 19052025 with no record of who or why. This matches the DVC/Snakemake principle that data state is derived, not edited (https://dl.acm.org/doi/10.1145/3589806.3600037).

ADR-004 diagnoses the identity bug correctly at the root (identity derived from filenames at many call sites) rather than patching symptoms, and fixes it at the right layer. Typed `SessionKey` + a ban on filename parsing outside the registry builder is stronger than the canonical-helper approach that demonstrably failed (78 ad-hoc `zfill(8)` sites vs 35 canonical calls).

S5's five-part provenance with the explicit rule that the *execution log is authoritative where it disagrees with the recorded code* is more sophisticated than standard provenance practice, and is the right lesson from a repo where 3,056 figures carry zero git sha.

ADR-013's `status` field including `retracted`/`refuted` as first-class, visible states exceeds normal field practice. Most labs bury retractions; publishing them in-repo is a genuine credibility asset.
Build order putting enforcement (sub-project 2) before the analysis port (3) is correct and counter-intuitive — gates written after the code they govern do get bent to fit it.

Sub-project −1 (secure work at risk before touching anything) was the right instinct and was executed; the memory note's tag-vs-remote verification gotcha is the kind of detail that separates a real backup from a claimed one.

The non-goals section is disciplined — explicitly refusing to re-derive science, rewrite third-party pipelines, or build multi-user infrastructure keeps scope from metastasising in the places rebuilds usually die.

proposals.target: NEW-ADR (or §9 Risks + §3 Success criteria as S9)
proposals.title: Time box the rebuild with a stated stop-loss and a science-continues policy
proposals.detail: §9 lists six risks and none of them is 'this consumes four months and the paper does not get written'. Add an explicit budget per sub-project (calendar weeks and hours/week), a named stop-loss date, and a pre-agreed fallback: if sub-projects 1+2 are not demonstrably done by date X, scope collapses to the walking-skeleton path (registry + constants + provenance + one gate family) and everything else is ported lazily on first use. Also state what science continues during the rebuild and where it happens — currently `feature/early-lick-and-session-sorting` is 31 commits ahead of main and was committed today, so the answer is 'in the old repo', which nothing in the design acknowledges.
proposals.rationale: Realistic cost: 6 sub-projects × (spec → plan → build), 64 library modules, 19,268 LOC in the analysis package alone, 70-100 approval packets, plus bespoke AST gates, a registry, a generator, a provenance layer, a ledger and per-analysis nulls. That is plausibly 300-600 hours. AI assistance compresses the code but not the human-serial review, which is the binding constraint. A rebuild with no stop-loss and a paper deadline reliably ends as two half-repos — which is precisely how `docs/REFACTOR_PLAN.md` ended.
proposals.evidence: Measured 2026-08-07: `find src/visdetect -name '*.py' | grep -v __init__` = 64; `src/visdetect/analysis` = 40 files / 19,268 LOC; `git rev-list --count main..feature/early-lick-and-session-sorting` = 31, branch committed 2026-08-07. Design §9 risk table (lines 615-623) contains no schedule or scope risk. ADR-006 records that big-design-up-front already failed once here.

proposals.title: Gate on promotion to a claim, not on file creation — two explicit tiers
proposals.detail: Split the analysis contract into Tier 1 (explore) and Tier 2 (claim). Tier 1 requires only what the scaffold gives for free: session set from the registry, constants imported, output through the artefact API, layer declared, index entry. Tier 2 — triggered the moment an analysis's output is cited in a ledger row, a figure legend, a results doc or the paper — additionally requires the null control, synthetic recovery, pseudoreplication method, reuse statement, test, and the ADR-007 packet. Enforce it by making `ledger add` (ADR-013) refuse to write a row unless the Tier-2 artefacts exist and are current, instead of blocking commits.
proposals.rationale: Per-analysis Tier-2 overhead is roughly 8-25 h (pre-spec 0.5-1.5, reuse statement 0.3, offline test with fixtures 1-3, null implementation + runtime 1-2 plus compute, synthetic recovery 3-8, mixed-effects rework 1-3, packet 1-2, ADR-009 delta report 1-4 because it requires running the old code too). Against a 3-6 h exploratory analysis that is a 3-5x tax, and ~80% of exploratory analyses die without producing a claim. The design's stated escape — 'notebook/scratch paths are exempt by policy' (§9) — is unbounded: all 378 old scripts were scratch until one made a figure. Promotion-gating is also *more* robust against ADR-014's own motivating failure mode ('a rule that depends on remembering to apply it fails exactly when the result is exciting'), because the gate fires at the moment of excitement rather than at creation, when you do not yet know the result matters.
proposals.evidence: ADR-010 contract table (lines 336-350) has 14 rows; ADR-014 adds 2 more; ADR-013 adds a ledger row per claim. §9 line 622 states the scratch exemption without bounding it. Barriers to preregistration in animal research are documented as bureaucratic burden, time cost and low flexibility (https://journals.plos.org/plosbiology/article?id=10.1371/journal.pbio.3003905); registered-report advocates explicitly exempt purely exploratory work (https://metaror.org/article/evaluating-the-claim-that-preregistration-and-registered-reports-restrict-exploratory-research/).

proposals.title: Demote the AST structural-similarity gate to a periodic audit; keep the exact checks hard
proposals.detail: Keep as hard build-breaking gates only the two exact, zero-false-positive checks: the must-import registry (a local `def` of a registered name fails) and same-name-different-behaviour. Move 'no near-duplicate of existing library code' out of the commit path into a monthly / pre-milestone report that lists the top-N candidate pairs above threshold and requires triage (merge / justify / ignore-with-reason), recorded in one file. State the threshold is advisory and the report is the deliverable.
proposals.rationale: Type-3 near-miss clone detection has notoriously poor precision: reported precisions range from 10.5% (SimCad) to 80% (Oreo), with AST-similarity methods around 0.77 precision / 0.78 recall. In a neuroscience analysis library every per-session loop, every PSTH builder and every bootstrap wrapper is structurally near-identical by construction, so the false-positive rate here will be worse than published benchmarks. The design's own severity analysis says plain duplication only 'wastes effort and drifts' while same-name-different-behaviour 'silently corrupts comparisons' — a noisy gate on the benign class, blocking commits, is negative expected value and is the single most likely trigger for `--no-verify` habituation.
proposals.evidence: Clone-detector precision figures: https://arxiv.org/pdf/1812.05195 and https://arxiv.org/pdf/2401.09885. ADR-010 lines 358-367 make the severity split itself. The `partial_spearman` case (7 reimplementations, 3 mathematically different) is caught by the same-name rule, not by structural similarity.

proposals.title: Mandatory walking-skeleton milestone before specs 1-6 are signed off
proposals.detail: Insert milestone 0.5 between sub-project 0 and the Stage-2 spec session: one real session — deliberately the hardest identity case, a day-1-9 session such as 01072025 plus one BG_012 colliding-date twin — driven end to end through registry entry → typed `SessionKey` → canonical constants → load → one PSTH → one figure with a provenance sidecar → one ledger row → one gate run. Timebox 3-5 days. It does not replace spec-first; its output is an input to the Stage-2 session, and specs 1-6 must cite its measured ergonomics rather than assume them.
proposals.rationale: ADR-006 records the dissent (vertical-slice was recommended) and mitigates it only with an empirical audit — but the audit measures the *old* repo, not the new design's two riskiest and least-precedented decisions: the ergonomics of typed `SubjectID`/`SessionKey` at real call sites, and the shape of the five-part S5 provenance sidecar. Both are cheap to prototype and catastrophically expensive to change after six mutually-consistent specs cite them. A walking skeleton is the standard, cheap way to convert integration risk from a month-4 discovery into a week-1 one; typical skeletons run 2-4 weeks, and this one is smaller because it is foundation-only.
proposals.evidence: Walking-skeleton pattern and risk rationale: https://www.henricodolfing.ch/en/start-your-project-with-a-walking-skeleton/ and https://distilledpatterns.org/patterns/walking-skeleton/. Audit spec §8 resolved-question 3 already nominates BG_012 (9 colliding date-keys, 49 rows for 40 dates) as 'the hardest available test of the ADR-004 identity model' — that test should run against the model before six specs depend on it, not after.

proposals.title: Specify where each gate actually runs — several named 'CI gates' cannot run in CI
proposals.detail: S1, S2, S3, S5 and S6 each say 'CI gate fails on...', but the design never names a CI substrate, and the data (30.5 GB of pkls) is local to E: with heavy compute on Slurm. Add a three-tier table to ADR-003: (1) pre-commit — fast, source-only, seconds (shadow constants, filename parsing, layer imports, typed-id signatures, must-import registry, same-name-different-behaviour); (2) CI — source-only, full-repo, minutes (index freshness, CLAUDE.md regeneration diff, import-contract graph, packaging/clean-venv install for S8); (3) verification run — data-dependent, executed locally or on Slurm before a milestone or a ledger row, never per commit (null flatness, artefact provenance presence, registry staleness, ADR-009 difference reports). Anything in tier 3 is advisory-with-report, not build-breaking.
proposals.rationale: As written, at least four success criteria depend on gates that cannot see the data. If this is not settled now, the first sub-project-2 session will either invent a CI that skips half the checks (making S1-S6 aspirational) or attempt data-dependent CI on a Windows box and abandon it. Standard practice is fast checks pre-commit, slow ones pre-push/CI — that split has to be made explicitly, per gate.
proposals.evidence: Design lines 57-64 (S1-S6) all say 'CI gate' / 'check in CI'; §10 open questions asks only whether HPC job submission is in scope, never where CI runs. Repo has zero CI today (audit spec D5). Gate-tiering guidance: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gated_commit and https://nedspnt.medium.com/before-you-push-implementing-quality-gates-in-your-software-project-5d71645c72a0.

proposals.title: Re-scope the packet: the estimate is 2-3x low, and four of six sections should be generated
proposals.detail: Replace '20-40 approvals' with a measured count, and reduce per-packet cost rather than per-packet count. Auto-generate four of six sections from the code: Provenance (new/verbatim/ported — verbatim proven by an AST-hash equality check, not prose), Blast radius (from the import graph), How-we-know-it's-right (the check invocation and its captured stdout), and the ADR-009 delta table. The human writes only 'What it is' (one paragraph, plain language) and 'Decision'. Simultaneously raise granularity to coherent module *groups* or gate *families* where a group shares one spec, targeting ~15-25 packets.
proposals.rationale: The document's own alternatives analysis rejects layer-level review because 6-8 packets 'degrade into assent' and file-level because 100+ packets collapse from fatigue — but it priced module-granularity at 20-40. Measured, module-granularity is 70-100 (64 library modules today plus ~15-20 gates implied by ADR-003/010/014 plus the figures and AI layers), so the fatigue argument the ADR used against file-level now applies to its own choice. At 1-2 h each that is 100-200 h of pure ceremony. Generation preserves the rule 'no exemption for trivial' (a `parents[1]`/`parents[3]` slip is still caught, by the executed check) while removing the writing cost that causes the fatigue.
proposals.evidence: Measured 2026-08-07: 64 non-`__init__` modules under `src/visdetect` (core 9, analysis 40, anatomy 8, utils 3, viz 1, integrations 1, suite 5). ADR-003 names 6 gate classes, ADR-010 adds ~8 distinct enforcements, ADR-014 adds 2. ADR-007 alternatives at lines 241-244.

proposals.title: Make the packet adversarial by construction so the human arbitrates rather than assents
proposals.detail: Add a required section: 'Strongest objection found, and its resolution' — produced by an independent adversarial pass (a second agent, or the project's existing `harden-result` battery convention) before the packet reaches the human. The human then reads a disagreement with a proposed resolution, not a proposal. If the adversarial pass finds nothing, that is stated explicitly and is itself reviewable.
proposals.rationale: ADR-007 rests on the claim that 'a human who understands the science is the only reliable check'. But the human is one person, mid-project, reviewing packets authored by the assistant that built the thing, at a rate of tens per month. The realistic approval rate approaches 100% and the gate becomes a signature. The project already has the right instinct codified in memory (`feedback_adversarial_review_and_run_tests_complementary`, the `harden-result` skill) — apply it to construction, which is exactly what ADR-007 says it is doing with the execution rule, but applied to judgment as well as to output.
proposals.evidence: ADR-007 lines 248-250. Project convention `feedback_verify_important_results_adversarially` and the repo's `harden-result` skill already mandate adversarial multi-agent verification for results; ADR-007 imports the execution rule from that convention but not the adversarial one.

proposals.title: A single sanctioned, logged override — and ban --no-verify at the harness level
proposals.detail: Every gate must emit four things on failure: the rule id, the ADR that motivated it, one line naming the historical defect it prevents, and the exact override syntax. Provide exactly one override: an inline `# gate-override: <rule-id> reason="..."` that the gate honours, appends to a git-tracked append-only `gate-overrides.log`, and that CI counts and reports per milestone. Concurrently deny `git commit --no-verify` via `permissions.deny` plus a PreToolUse hook, so the sanctioned path is the only path. Treat a persistently zero override count as a red flag (it means the gate is being routed around invisibly), and review the log at each milestone.
proposals.rationale: Nothing in the design says what happens when a future session — or a human collaborator — meets a failing bespoke AST gate they do not understand. The realistic outcomes are `--no-verify`, deleting the hook, or abandoning the commit; the first two reopen drift silently, which is the exact failure that killed the old repo's prose conventions. Industry practice for this is not prevention but logged, reviewed bypass. This is not hypothetical for an AI-assisted workflow: agents bypassing hooks with `--no-verify` despite explicit deny rules is a documented behaviour.
proposals.evidence: https://pydevtools.com/handbook/how-to/how-to-stop-ai-agents-from-bypassing-pre-commit-hooks/ and https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code/issues/40117 (agent bypasses hooks via --no-verify/stash despite deny rules); bypass-logging practice: https://xygeni.io/blog/why-pre-commit-hooks-fail-at-stopping-secrets/. The design's only override statement is §9's unbounded 'notebook/scratch paths are exempt by policy'.

proposals.title: Old-repo freeze needs a per-branch disposition table produced at the END of sub-project 0
proposals.detail: §9 says the old repo is 'frozen at a tagged commit at the start of sub-project 3' with no policy for what is in flight. Add a deliverable to sub-project 0: a disposition table with one row per live branch and per untracked working-tree file — merge to main before freeze / port to the new repo / abandon with a recorded reason. Add a hard rule: no new branches in the old repo after the freeze date. Explicitly decide the QC1 alignment repair, which is simultaneously a known-defect register entry and live uncommitted code.
proposals.rationale: Measured today there are 63 unmerged commits across 5 branches (early-lick 31 ahead, camera-tagger 21, population-field 4, fa-psth-and-manifest-sort 3 — which holds the live session-sort fix, fig5eh 4), and the QC1 repair scripts are *untracked* in the working tree of the design branch itself. A freeze declared 'at the start of sub-project 3' with that much in flight either strands the work or gets quietly ignored, and the manifest-sort fix on `hardening/fa-psth-and-manifest-sort` is already a defect fix living only on an unmerged branch — exactly the pattern the rebuild exists to end.
proposals.evidence: Measured 2026-08-07 via `git rev-list --count main..<branch>`: early-lick-and-session-sorting 31, camera-tagger-2b 21, population-field-plan2 4, hardening/fa-psth-and-manifest-sort 3, fig5eh-preparatory-cellclass 4. `git status --short` shows untracked `scripts/QC_technical/characterize_unsolvable_alignment.py` and `validate_event_spike_clock_drift.py`. Design §9 line 619; §6 line 545 names the QC1 repair as a known defect.

proposals.title: Define a port sunset criterion — 'the port is done when...' — and a cold-storage tier
proposals.detail: State that the port is complete when the modules required to regenerate the named figure set of the impulsivity-plus-sensitivity paper have landed. Everything else goes to one of two lists: the audit's existing `drop-list.md`, or a new `cold-list.md` — old-repo modules that remain readable and are ported lazily on first use, never proactively. Name a target v1 port budget (e.g. ≤12 modules) in the ADR so the Stage-2 specs are written against it.
proposals.rationale: S1-S8 define done per criterion but nothing defines when the *port* ends. With 40 analysis modules at 19,268 LOC and ADR-009 demanding a per-component attributed difference report each time, an unbounded port becomes a permanent second job that competes directly with writing the paper. A named figure set is the only stopping rule that is both computable and aligned with the project's actual goal.
proposals.evidence: Measured: `src/visdetect/analysis` = 40 modules, 19,268 LOC. ADR-009 lines 321-324 require a difference report per component. §3 success criteria and §10 open questions contain no completion definition for sub-project 3. Audit spec §4 already produces `drop-list.md`, so `cold-list.md` is a one-line addition to an existing deliverable.

proposals.title: Move the minimal artefact/provenance API into the foundation — sub-project 2 has undeclared forward dependencies on 4
proposals.detail: The dependency table says sub-project 2 (enforcement) depends on 1 only. But ADR-010's contract row 'Outputs written through the artefact API' is enforced by 'artefact without provenance fails (S5)', and ADR-014's null gate needs a convention for where a null result is stored and how its currency is checked — both of which live in the figures/artefacts layer, sub-project 4. Move the minimal provenance-sidecar writer and artefact-path API into sub-project 1, leaving only the plot system and palettes in 4, and update the dependency column accordingly.
proposals.rationale: As specified, sub-project 2 cannot implement two of its own gates without machinery that does not exist for two more sub-projects. Under ADR-006 no earlier execution catches this, so it surfaces mid-build as either a stubbed gate that never gets un-stubbed or a scope-creep merge of 4 into 2. The cross-spec consistency pass is meant to find contradictions like this, but it runs after all six specs are written — naming it now is free.
proposals.evidence: Design §7 table lines 568-577 (sub-project 2 'Depends on 1'; sub-project 4 'Depends on 3'). ADR-010 line 339 and ADR-014 point 1 (lines 508-512) both require artefact-layer machinery. This is precisely the class of defect ADR-006's mitigation acknowledges it cannot catch by execution.

proposals.title: Replace the dormant loader-refusal guard with a session-access log
proposals.detail: Keep the `cohort` registry field — that part is genuinely impossible to retrofit. But drop the loader machinery that refuses to serve confirmatory sessions, since as of 2026-08-07 every session is `discovery` and the guard therefore has zero live callers and will bit-rot unnoticed. Replace it with a session-access log: every analysis run records which sessions it touched, written alongside the S5 provenance sidecar. This is cheap, useful immediately as the 'inputs' component of provenance, and is what actually makes a later confirmatory split defensible — you can then prove a candidate held-out set appears in zero prior analyses.
proposals.rationale: This does not relitigate the deferral decision, which is a correct power judgement. It observes that the mechanism chosen to preserve future optionality is the wrong one: an untested guard with no users provides no assurance in 2027, whereas an access log accumulating from day one provides exactly the evidence a future confirmatory claim needs. It also gives the deferral its missing teeth — ADR-012 admits the forking-paths risk 'is real and remains open', and an access log is the cheapest partial mitigation available.
proposals.evidence: ADR-012 lines 437-466, particularly line 440 ('As of 2026-08-07 every session is discovery') and lines 459-466 (the stated open risk). S5 (line 61) already requires 'inputs (registry snapshot + decision-log revision)' — the access log is a strict refinement of a component already mandated.

proposals.title: Narrow 'estimator' or the synthetic-recovery rule will be ignored wholesale
proposals.detail: Define estimator explicitly as: anything that fits latent parameters, or produces a scalar the paper interprets as a property of a neuron, session or subject (kernel width, DDM drift/threshold/start-point, coding-direction angle, decoder weight, state occupancy). Explicitly exclude standard statistics taken from established libraries (bootstrap CI, permutation test, FDR, partial Spearman, AUROC). Allow recovery to be demonstrated once per estimator *family* and reused, rather than per analysis.
proposals.rationale: As written, 'every new estimator demonstrates parameter recovery on synthetic data' plausibly applies to a bootstrap wrapper, which is absurd and will get the whole rule mentally filed as unenforceable — and a narrow rule obeyed beats a broad rule ignored. The ADR itself concedes this is 'the largest ongoing cost of any ADR here'. Narrowing preserves every case that motivates it: the TF-pulse circularity bug, the kernel-width estimator, the DDM fits.
proposals.evidence: ADR-014 lines 513-514 and 532-534. The design's own worked examples of estimator failure (TF-pulse PETH circularity, the raw-Hz transient/sustained artifact) all fall inside the narrow definition; none is a standard library statistic.

proposals.title: Bound the ledger backfill: start empty, migrate only paper claims plus every retraction
proposals.detail: State that the ledger covers claims made from the new repo forward. The one-time migration is exactly two sets: (a) claims that appear in the paper outline, and (b) every already-retracted or refuted claim — of which there are about four, and which are the highest-value rows in the whole ledger. Do not backfill exploratory findings from memory notes or historic results docs.
proposals.rationale: 'One versioned ledger holds every claim the project makes' reads, against 11 results docs (several 240-270 lines) and ~60 memory notes, as 60-150 backfilled rows each requiring effect size, CI and a verification record — a multi-day task that must complete before the ledger is trustworthy, and which will therefore not happen. Bounding it makes the ledger real on day one and preserves its two genuine functions: making retractions visible, and making analysis multiplicity countable going forward.
proposals.evidence: Measured: `docs/science/` holds 11 results documents (2026-07-02-B10-RESULTS-explained.md 241 lines, transient-sustained-spectrum 269, transient-sustained-tf-cells 239). MEMORY.md indexes ~60 notes. ADR-013 line 470 ('every claim the project makes') and line 502.

proposals.title: State the disposition of the 36 GB FIGURES and 15.9 GB cache tree — 'preserve' is not a plan
proposals.detail: §9 says artefact preservation is a sub-project 6 deliverable 'executed before any deletion' but never says where 52 GB goes. Since ADR-008 bans junctions and git cannot hold it, the honest design is: the old tree becomes a read-only archive root, referenced by the new repo's configured data root; tracked deliverable figures migrate; the ~3,000 untracked figures stay in the archive and are deleted only after submission. Say this explicitly, and acknowledge that it means the old directory is not deletable at 'decommission'. Separately, move the four irreplaceable hand-made files (~27 KB: 217 hand-drawn state episodes, 133 blinded session sorts, `rules.md` + `state_rule.pkl`, pupil sidecars) into git with `git add -f` now, in sub-project −1, not at migration.
proposals.rationale: Sub-project 6 is named 'Migration & decommission' but the only irreversible artefacts in the project cannot be migrated and cannot be decommissioned, and the four files that genuinely cannot be regenerated by any rerun still exist on exactly one disk. Leaving both unstated invites the migration session to improvise, which for the hand-labels means a coin flip against permanent loss.
proposals.evidence: Audit spec D4 (16,779 cache files / 15.9 GB; 3,056 figures / 36.1 GB), §8 'Still open' (the four hand-made files, ~27 KB, gitignored, one disk). Memory note: only off-tree copy is `e:\python_analysis\_handlabel_backup_20260806`, same physical disk. ADR-008 forbids junctions; §9 line 620 says 'preserve' without a destination.

proposals.title: Isolate generated content in its own file so a stale generation is not a merge conflict with prose
proposals.detail: Put the generated factual sections in a separate `CLAUDE.generated.md` (or a single clearly fenced `<!-- BEGIN generated -->` block) that the hand-written CLAUDE.md references. Make the CI failure message name the exact one-command fix (`py -m visdetect.tools.gen_claude_md --write`). Keep the generated table deliberately short — a constants table and a module map, not a mirror of the codebase.
proposals.rationale: The failure mode nobody modelled: the generator becomes bespoke machinery that itself breaks during a refactor, and the CI message 'regeneration produced a diff' arrives at the worst possible moment, interleaved with hand-written prose in one file. Separating generated from hand-written makes staleness visible and the fix mechanical, and prevents the generator from becoming a blocker on unrelated work. Note also that the old CLAUDE.md's worst property — 18% of it describing a directory deleted in July 2026 — was a *prose* problem the generator does not solve; ADR-005 should say what keeps the prose half honest (a dead-path check over every path named in prose, which the audit already builds for D6).
proposals.evidence: ADR-005 lines 176-181; S6 line 62. Audit spec D6 already specifies a dead-path count over 'every path, directory and script named in docs or skills' — promote that check into the ADR-005 gate set so the hand-written half has an enforcement story too.

overbuilt: The AST near-duplicate gate as a build-breaking commit gate (ADR-010). Published Type-3 clone-detector precision spans 10.5%-80%; in an analysis library where every per-session loop looks alike it will be worse. Keep the exact must-import registry and the same-name-different-behaviour ban (both zero-false-positive, and the latter is the genuinely corrupting case by the design's own analysis); ship duplication as a monthly triage report.

Module-granularity approval packets at the measured count. ADR-007 estimates 20-40; the live repo implies 70-100 (64 library modules + ~15-20 gates + figures + AI layer). Generate four of the six sections from code and bundle into module groups → ~15-25 packets at a fraction of the cost each.

Running null controls in CI plus tracking whether each stored null is 'current with respect to the analysis code' (ADR-014 point 1). Currency-tracking over code + inputs is a miniature build system. Simplify: the null result file must exist and must record the code sha it was computed under; staleness is a warning surfaced in a periodic report, and only blocks at the moment a ledger row cites the analysis.

Synthetic parameter recovery for 'every new estimator' as literally written (ADR-014 point 2). Narrow to latent-parameter fits and paper-interpreted scalars, and allow one demonstration per estimator family. As written it nominally covers bootstrap wrappers and will be discarded wholesale.

ADR-012's loader-refusal guard. Every session is `discovery`, so the guard has zero callers, will never be exercised, and provides no assurance at activation time. Keep the registry field, drop the guard, add a session-access log instead.
Backfilling the ADR-013 ledger across all historic claims (11 results docs, ~60 memory notes → 60-150 rows). Start forward-only; migrate only paper claims and the ~4 retractions/refutations.

Triple approval per module: the Stage-2 spec approves it, the ADR-007 packet approves it again, and ADR-009's delta report gates it a third time. Collapse the first two — let the spec supply the packet's 'what it is', 'why it exists' and 'provenance' sections verbatim, so the packet adds only the executed check, the attributed delta, and the decision.

ADR-010's pre-specification requirement applied to every analysis. Keep it for Tier-2 claims where it is real preregistration; for exploratory work it produces rubber-stamped predictions written after the first look, which is worse than an honest `post-hoc` label in the ledger row.
open_questions: What is the paper's figure list? Without it there is no computable sunset criterion for the port, and ADR-009's per-component difference report is demanded an unbounded number of times.

Where does CI actually run, and on what OS? Windows local, a Linux runner, or Slurm? Several S1-S6 gates are data-dependent and cannot run wherever the answer is, which means the design's central enforcement claim is currently unlocated.

Who reviews an ADR-007 packet when the author (the assistant) and the approver (the sole researcher) are the only two parties, and the approver commissioned the work? Realistic approval rate approaches 100% unless the packet is made adversarial by construction.
What is the total time budget, and what science is allowed to continue during the rebuild? Five branches are currently live, one committed today, with 63 unmerged commits between them.

Does the QC1 alignment repair — currently untracked files in the design branch's working tree — land in the old repo before freeze, or move to the new repo's alignment module? It is simultaneously a known-defect register entry and in-flight code, and the register cannot be finalised until this is decided.

What happens to the ~28 analysis modules that fall outside the paper's figure set? Cold storage, drop, or indefinite port backlog — the answer determines whether sub-project 3 is a 6-week or a 6-month task.

How is the ADR-010 template kept in sync with the gates in practice? The stated mitigation ('generated from the same source') is the right principle, but no ADR names the artefact that is the shared source, and if it does not exist the template drifts exactly as CLAUDE.md's constants table did.

If the walking-skeleton milestone finds that typed `SessionKey` is unacceptably verbose at call sites, or that the five-part provenance sidecar is impractical to write per figure, is there a defined path to amend ADR-004 / S5 — or does the immutability rule ('to change one, add a superseding record') make early empirical correction feel like failure?
